questions.trap_type: Positive present 'to be' ('is') → negative question tag. IS → isn't it.
questions.learning_tip: Positive present 'to be' → negative tag. Helping others IS rewarding, ISN'T it? POSITIVE → NEGATIVE. IS → ISN'T. Tag questions match the auxiliary verb of the main clause.

questions.stem: The students painted the community centre walls ________ to brighten up the neighbourhood.
questions.trap_type: 'The students' = they = plural third person → reflexive = themselves. 'Ourself' does not exist; 'himself/herself' are singular.
questions.learning_tip: 'The students' = THEY (plural, third person). Reflexive = THEMSELVES. They did it THEMSELVES = without outside help.

questions.stem: Although it was raining, ________ volunteers still turned up for the beach clean-up drive.
questions.trap_type: 'Volunteers' is countable. 'Little' and 'much' are for uncountable nouns. 'Many' = a large number of countable things.
questions.learning_tip: MANY + countable plural: many volunteers, many students. MUCH / LITTLE = for uncountable things. Volunteers = countable → MANY.

C.label: Section C – Grammar Cloze (Verb forms of 'help')

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Sara loves (1)________ people in her community.' Signal: 'loves + ___' = gerund (verb-ing). Pattern: love + verb-ing → helping.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'to help' instead of the gerund after 'loves'.
questions.learning_tip: LOVE + verb-ing: loves HELPING people. After 'loves', always add -ING.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'She (2)________ at the food bank every Saturday.' Signal: 'every Saturday' = regular habit = simple present. Subject 'She' = singular → helps.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'help' (plural form) forgetting that 'She' is a singular subject.
questions.learning_tip: 'Every Saturday' = habit = simple present. She (singular) → HELPS at the food bank.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Last month, she (3)________ to pack over five hundred meal boxes.' Signal: 'Last month' = past. 'Help' is regular: help → helped.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'help' (base form) ignoring the past time signal 'Last month'.
questions.learning_tip: 'Last month' = past. 'Help' is regular: help → HELPED.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'While she (4)________ an elderly volunteer sort the food, she heard many stories.' Signal: 'While she ___' = ongoing background action in the past. Subject 'she' = singular → was helping. Interrupted by 'she heard'.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'helped' (simple past) missing the ongoing background signal 'while she'.
questions.learning_tip: 'While she ___' = ongoing background past action = past continuous. She WAS HELPING when she heard the stories.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Several other students (5)________ with the packing on that same day.' Signal: same past time frame, plural subject 'several other students' + ongoing parallel action → were helping.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'helped' (simple past) instead of the past continuous for an ongoing parallel action.
questions.learning_tip: Several students = plural. They were doing it at the same time = WERE HELPING (past continuous).

questions.context_check: Passage: 'It feels good (6)________ others.' Signal: 'feels good + ___' = infinitive. Pattern: It feels good + to + base verb. The word 'to' is already written before the blank in the passage, so the answer is the base form 'help'.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'helping' instead of the base verb form that follows 'to' (already written in the passage).
questions.learning_tip: 'It feels good TO + base verb': It feels good to HELP others. The word 'to' is already there, so just write the base verb.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Sara always says she wants (7)________ as many people as possible.' Signal: 'wants + ___' = infinitive. Pattern: want + to + base verb → to help.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'helping' instead of the infinitive that follows 'wants'.
questions.learning_tip: 'Want TO + base verb': wants TO HELP as many people as possible. Always use the infinitive after 'wants'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Right now, she (8)________ a group of new volunteers settle in on their first day.' Signal: 'Right now' = present continuous. Subject 'she' = singular → is helping.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'helps' (simple present habit) missing the 'right now' signal for present continuous.
questions.learning_tip: 'Right now' = present continuous. She (singular) → IS HELPING a group of new volunteers.

C.passage: Sara loves (1)________ people in her community. She (2)________ at the food bank every Saturday without fail. Last month, she (3)________ to pack over five hundred meal boxes for needy families. While she (4)________ an elderly volunteer sort the canned food, she heard many moving stories about the people they were serving. Several other students (5)________ with the packing on that same day. Sara always says it feels good to (6)________ others, no matter how small the act. She always says she wants (7)________ as many people as possible. Right now, she (8)________ a group of new volunteers settle in on their first day.

D.label: Section D – Vocabulary Cloze
D.passage: Kindness can change a person's day. A (1)________ act — giving up a seat, holding open a door — takes little effort but means a great deal. People who (2)________ others often describe feeling happier themselves. In communities where residents look out for each other, there is a strong sense of (3)________ — a feeling of belonging and shared responsibility. Schools often teach students to show (4)________ — understanding and sharing the feelings of others. Even a small (5)________ like a smile or a thank-you note can brighten someone's entire day.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'offered' which is not in the box. VOLUNTEERED = freely offered to do something without being paid.
questions.learning_tip: VOLUNTEERED = freely offered to do something to help, without being paid or asked. Students VOLUNTEERED their time.

questions.trap_type: 'Selfless' = thinking about others before yourself. Students may confuse with 'generous' which is not in the box.
questions.learning_tip: SELFLESS = thinking about others before yourself. Giving up your Saturday to help others for free = a SELFLESS act.

questions.trap_type: Students confuse 'grateful' (feeling thankful) with 'appreciated' (blank 5, recognised as valuable).
questions.learning_tip: GRATEFUL = feeling thankful for something. The organisers are GRATEFUL = they feel thankful for the students' help.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'difference' which is not in the box. IMPACT = a strong effect on something or someone.
questions.learning_tip: IMPACT = a strong effect on something or someone. Making a big IMPACT = having a significant positive effect on people's lives.

questions.trap_type: By elimination after 'grateful' is used in blank 3. APPRECIATED = recognised as valuable.
questions.learning_tip: APPRECIATED = recognised as valuable and good. His work was APPRECIATED = others saw it as important and were thankful for it.

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — here (place) vs hear (to listen)
questions.trap_type: 'here' (place) when 'hear' (ears) is needed.
questions.learning_tip: HEAR = detect sound with ears. HERE = at this place. 'We could HEAR the excitement' → use ears? YES → HEAR. HEAR = ears. HERE = location.

questions.error_type: Simple past — organise → organised (not base form)
questions.trap_type: 'organize' is base/present form. Past tense context requires 'organised'.
questions.learning_tip: In a past tense context (the event began), use PAST TENSE. ORGANISE → ORGANISED (add -d). 'One student organize all the boxes' = WRONG in past context. Use ORGANISED.

questions.error_type: Irregular past — bring → brought (not brings present tense)
questions.trap_type: 'brings' is present tense. Past tense context requires 'brought'.
questions.learning_tip: BRING → BROUGHT (irregular past). In a past tense context, use BROUGHT. 'Some volunteers brings' = WRONG — wrong tense AND wrong form. BRING → BROUGHT. Irregular — memorise it!

questions.error_type: Subject-verb agreement — plural subject (the tables)
questions.trap_type: 'The tables' is plural. Students write 'was'.
questions.learning_tip: Plural subject → plural verb! The TABLES WERE arranged = TABLES is plural → WERE. WAS is only for ONE thing. Find the main noun: TABLES = plural → WERE.

questions.error_type: Possessive apostrophe — plural possessive (organisers', not organiser's's)
questions.trap_type: Students double the apostrophe/s.
questions.learning_tip: Plural possessive: ORGANISERS' sign-off sheet = the sheet belonging to all the organisers. NEVER 'organiser's's'. Singular: organiser's. Plural: organisers'. One apostrophe + no extra -s for plurals ending in -s.

E.passage: Last Saturday, our school organised a charity drive to help the elderly residents in our neighbourhood. We could here (1) the excitement in the school hall as students registered for their volunteer roles. One student organize (2) all the collection boxes and labels before the event began. Some volunteers brings (3) homemade cookies and snacks to share during the lunch break. The tables was (4) arranged in a circle so everyone could see and speak to each other easily. At the end, the organiser's's (5) sign-off sheet was checked before the items were sent to the charity home.

questions.sentence_a: The community leader asked the volunteers a question.
questions.sentence_b: Did you enjoy helping at the charity event?
questions.instruction: Combine into one sentence using reported speech. Begin: 'The community leader asked...'
questions.model_answer: The community leader asked the volunteers if they enjoyed helping at the charity event.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'asked if did they enjoy' (wrong order) or keep 'you'.
questions.learning_tip: YES/NO question → reported speech: ASKED + IF + subject + verb (normal order). 'Did YOU enjoy?' → asked IF THEY ENJOYED. Pronoun: you → they. Tense: did enjoy → enjoyed. Word order is normal after 'if'.

questions.sentence_a: The girl noticed the old woman struggling with her bags.
questions.sentence_b: She immediately offered to help.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'when'.
questions.model_answer: When the girl noticed the old woman struggling with her bags, she immediately offered to help.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'The girl noticed the old woman struggling when she immediately offered to help' — wrong order.
questions.learning_tip: WHEN + [triggering event], [resulting action]. When she NOTICED, she OFFERED to help. The noticing always comes first in the 'when' clause.

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage:
Ten-year-old Reuben was walking to school on a rainy Tuesday when he spotted an old man sitting on the ground near the post office. The man's cane slipped out of his reach and he could not get up on his own.

Reuben stopped and looked around. Several adults walked past without stopping. Reuben hesitated for a moment — he was already running late for school.

Then he made his decision. He walked over, picked up the cane and handed it to the man. Then he gently held the man's arm and helped him to his feet.

'Thank you, young man,' the old man said breathlessly. 'My name is Mr Wong. I live just around the corner.'

Reuben walked Mr Wong home, even though it added ten minutes to his journey. When he finally arrived at school, his teacher noticed he was late. Reuben explained what happened.

The teacher said nothing for a moment. Then she smiled and said, 'The bell can wait. Some things are more important than being on time.'

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 2 has the same meaning as 'helped someone feel less sad or worried'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: 'Surprised' = astonished; 'confused' = puzzled; 'ignored' = paid no attention. COMFORTED = helped someone feel less distressed.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: COMFORTED = helped someone feel less sad, scared or worried. Mei COMFORTED Mr Wong = she said or did things to ease his distress. COMFORT = the noun (a source of relief); COMFORTED = the past tense verb.

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does 'it' refer to in 'she had not expected it'?

options.1: The bag of groceries Mr Wong was carrying
options.2: The strong grip of Mr Wong's hand as he thanked her — a sign of how much her help meant to him

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking 'it' = the groceries. But 'had not expected IT' = an emotional response she did not anticipate.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: PRONOUN REFERENCE: 'she had not expected IT.' What surprised her? Not the groceries — but MR WONG'S STRONG HANDSHAKE and the EMOTION behind it. IT = the depth of his gratitude, expressed through that firm grip.

mcq_questions.stem: Why does the writer end the passage by saying Mei 'decided she would come back next week'?

options.1: Because Mei had not finished her task and needed to return.
options.2: Because one act of kindness made Mei realise the value of helping, and she wanted to continue.
options.3: Because Mr Wong asked her to come back.
options.4: Because her teacher told her she had to visit the elderly every week.

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 3 or 4 thinking someone told her to return. The decision is Mei's own choice, driven by her experience.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: INFERENCE: Mei's decision to COME BACK is entirely her OWN — driven by the feeling she experienced when she helped Mr Wong. This shows that ONE ACT OF KINDNESS created a desire to continue helping. Option 2 = the passage's central message about how helping transforms the helper too.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 1, is it True or False that Mei planned to help Mr Wong? Give a reason.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: False. The passage says Mei saw Mr Wong by chance while on her way home — she did not plan to help him, it happened unexpectedly.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 1: Mei SAW MR WONG BY CHANCE on her way home. She had not planned to help — it was a spontaneous act. Answer is FALSE.

open_ended_questions.stem: What TWO things did Reuben do to help the old man get up?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) He picked up the cane and handed it to the man. (ii) He gently held the man's arm and helped him to his feet.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students give only one action or describe him walking Mr Wong home, which is a separate later action.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 3: (1) he PICKED UP THE CANE and gave it to the man, (2) he HELD THE MAN'S ARM and helped him up. Both are in paragraph 3.

open_ended_questions.stem: How do we know Reuben put Mr Wong's needs before his own? Give TWO pieces of evidence from the passage.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) He stopped to help even though he was already running late for school. (ii) He walked Mr Wong home, which added ten more minutes to his journey.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students give the same reason twice, or mention only one of Reuben's two sacrifices.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Two separate sacrifices: (1) he helped even though already LATE; (2) he walked Mr Wong home = TEN MORE MINUTES added. These are two distinct pieces of evidence.

open_ended_questions.stem: What does the word 'breathlessly' in paragraph 4 tell us about Mr Wong at that moment?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: It tells us that Mr Wong was out of breath, probably from the effort of struggling to get up from the ground.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'he was happy' and ignore the physical condition the word describes.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: 'Breathlessly' = speaking while out of breath. Mr Wong was struggling to get up, so he was still breathing hard when he finally spoke.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on her actions throughout the passage, describe TWO character traits of Mei with evidence.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) EMPATHETIC: when Mei saw Mr Wong struggling with his groceries, she immediately understood his difficulty and offered to help — showing she was sensitive to others' needs. (ii) SELFLESS: she gave up her own time without being asked, expecting nothing in return, and then decided to come back the following week.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'kind and helpful' without precise traits or textual evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: TRAIT INFERENCE: EMPATHETIC = saw Mr Wong STRUGGLING, immediately offered help. SELFLESS = gave up her time, expected NOTHING IN RETURN, decided to COME BACK. Name trait + evidence = full marks.

questions.stem: In the photography club, the best photographs were as ________ as paintings — every detail perfectly captured and composed.
questions.trap_type: 'Blurry' and 'ordinary' describe poor or unremarkable photos. 'Dark' = lacking light. BEAUTIFUL = aesthetically pleasing and impressive.
questions.learning_tip: AS + adj + AS = Simile! The photographs were AS BEAUTIFUL AS paintings = comparing the quality of the photos to artwork. BEAUTIFUL = visually pleasing and impressive. AS + ADJECTIVE + AS is the correct simile form.

questions.stem: My brother ________ his stamp collection every weekend, carefully arranging the stamps by country and year.
questions.trap_type: 'Threw away', 'destroyed' and 'lost' are all negative actions. Only 'organised' = arranged neatly.
questions.learning_tip: ORGANISED = arranged in a neat and logical order. He ORGANISED his stamps by country = sorted and arranged them carefully.

questions.stem: Kai spent the whole weekend trying to ________ the broken model ship he had accidentally knocked over.
questions.trap_type: 'Give up on' = stop trying; 'put off' = delay; 'run away from' = flee. FIX UP = repair or restore something that is damaged.
questions.learning_tip: PHRASAL VERB: FIX UP = repair or restore something damaged or in poor condition. Kai tried to FIX UP the broken model ship = he worked to put it back together. FIX + UP work together as one meaning.

questions.stem: When Mei's photograph won the school competition and was printed in the newsletter, she was ________ — it was the happiest moment of her school year.
questions.trap_type: 'Under the weather' = ill; 'in hot water' = trouble; 'at a loss' = confused. OVER THE MOON = extremely happy.
questions.learning_tip: IDIOM: OVER THE MOON = feeling extremely happy and delighted. Mei was OVER THE MOON = her happiness was at its very highest when she won. Idioms cannot be understood word by word!

questions.stem: The gardener ________ the overgrown rose bushes so that new, healthy flowers could grow in spring.
questions.trap_type: 'Watered' and 'planted' add to plants. 'Buried' = put underground. Only 'pruned' = trimmed back to encourage new growth.
questions.learning_tip: PRUNED = carefully trimmed back the extra branches of a plant so it grows stronger and produces more flowers.

questions.stem: Nobody in the photography club ________ how to use a darkroom — it is a skill that very few people still practise.
questions.trap_type: NOBODY = singular → verb+S.
questions.learning_tip: NOBODY / EVERYONE / SOMEONE = Singular! Nobody KNOWS how to use a darkroom = add -S. 'Nobody know' is WRONG. Singular indefinite pronouns always take singular present-tense verbs.

questions.stem: Mei has ________ over three hundred photographs since she joined the school photography club last January.
questions.trap_type: HAS + past participle = present perfect. TAKE → TAKEN (irregular).
questions.learning_tip: HAS + past participle = present perfect. Mei HAS TAKEN three hundred photographs = started since January and still going. TAKE → TAKEN (irregular past participle). HAS + TAKEN = present perfect.

questions.stem: Kai ________ a kite by the river when it suddenly snapped and flew into the trees.
questions.trap_type: 'The kite snapped' = sudden interrupting event. Kai was already flying it = past continuous.
questions.learning_tip: The kite SNAPPED = sudden past event. Kai was already in the middle of flying it = WAS FLYING (past continuous). Was/were + verb-ing = action in progress when interrupted.

questions.stem: Mei's latest photograph is far ________ than any picture she took when she first joined the club.
questions.trap_type: 'Clearest' = superlative; 'more clearer' is WRONG. CLEARER = comparative of 'clear'.
questions.learning_tip: Short adjective + -ER = comparative. Clear → CLEARER. Mei's latest photo is CLEARER THAN her earlier ones = comparing two photos. 'More clearer' is ALWAYS WRONG — never add BOTH 'more' AND '-er'.

questions.stem: The library was very quiet ________ many children were reading silently at their tables.
questions.trap_type: The library was quiet AT THE TIME when children were reading. 'When' connects the state to the moment it occurred.
questions.learning_tip: The library was quiet WHEN children were reading = the quietness and the reading happened at the same time. WHEN connects two simultaneous events.

questions.stem: Having a hobby is important for your mental wellbeing, ________ it?
questions.trap_type: Positive present 'to be' ('is') → negative question tag. IS → isn't it.
questions.learning_tip: Positive present 'to be' → negative tag. Having a hobby IS important, ISN'T it? POSITIVE → NEGATIVE. IS → ISN'T. Tag questions: match the 'to be' verb of the main clause.

questions.stem: My sister enjoys reading ________ she often finishes a whole book in a single afternoon.
questions.trap_type: Cause-effect: enjoys reading = cause → finishes books quickly = result. 'So' links cause to result.
questions.learning_tip: She enjoys reading SO she finishes books quickly. Enjoyment (cause) → finishing fast (result). Cause + SO + result.

questions.stem: The photography club members took ________ cameras to the nature reserve last Sunday.
questions.trap_type: Before 'cameras' (a noun), use a possessive adjective. 'They' is a subject pronoun and cannot describe a noun.
questions.learning_tip: Before 'cameras' (a noun), use a POSSESSIVE ADJECTIVE: THEIR cameras. 'They cameras' is wrong.

C.label: Section C – Grammar Cloze (Verb forms of 'read')

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Nadia loves (1)________ adventure books.' Signal: 'loves + ___' = gerund (verb-ing). Pattern: love + verb-ing → reading.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'to read' instead of the gerund after 'loves'.
questions.learning_tip: LOVE + verb-ing: loves READING adventure books. After 'loves', always add -ING.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'She (2)________ at least one book a week during the school term.' Signal: 'during the school term' = regular habit = simple present. Subject 'She' = singular → reads.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'read' (plural form) forgetting that 'She' is a singular subject.
questions.learning_tip: A regular habit = simple present. She (singular) → READS at least one book a week.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Last holidays, she (3)________ over ten books in just three weeks.' Signal: 'Last holidays' = past. 'Read' is irregular: present = read ('reed'), past = read ('red'). Same spelling, different pronunciation.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'readed', not knowing 'read' is irregular in the past tense.
questions.learning_tip: 'Read' is irregular: read (present, 'reed') → read (past, 'red'). Same spelling, different pronunciation. 'Last holidays' = past → READ (pronounced 'red').

questions.context_check: Passage: 'While she (4)________ in the garden, a butterfly landed on the page.' Signal: 'While she ___' = ongoing background action in the past. Subject 'she' = singular → was reading. Interrupted by 'a butterfly landed'.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'read' (simple past) missing the ongoing background signal 'while she'.
questions.learning_tip: 'While she ___' in the garden = ongoing background past action = past continuous. She WAS READING when the butterfly landed.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Several of her friends (5)________ the same series that same week.' Signal: same past time frame, plural subject 'several of her friends' + ongoing parallel action → were reading.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'read' (simple past) instead of the past continuous for an ongoing parallel action.
questions.learning_tip: Several friends = plural. They were reading at the same time = WERE READING (past continuous).

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Their teacher reminded them (6)________ at least thirty minutes a day.' Signal: 'reminded them + ___' = infinitive. Pattern: remind someone + to + base verb → to read.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'reading' instead of the infinitive after 'reminded them'.
questions.learning_tip: 'Reminded them TO + base verb': reminded them TO READ at least thirty minutes a day.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Nadia sometimes likes to (7)________ her favourite stories when she misses the characters.' Signal: 'likes to + ___' = base verb after infinitive marker 'to'. Meaning: read again = reread. The word 'to' is already written before the blank.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'reading' or 'read' without noticing the meaning of reading a book again = reread.
questions.learning_tip: REREAD = read something again. Nadia REREADS her favourite stories = reads them a second or third time. 'To' is already there → use the base form: reread.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Right now, Nadia (8)________ her favourite book to her baby sister before bedtime.' Signal: 'Right now' = present continuous. Subject 'Nadia' = singular → is reading.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'reads' (simple present habit) missing the 'right now' signal for present continuous.
questions.learning_tip: 'Right now' = present continuous. Nadia (singular) → IS READING her favourite book to her baby sister.

C.passage: Nadia loves (1)________ adventure books. She (2)________ at least one book a week during the school term. Last holidays, she (3)________ over ten books in just three weeks. While she (4)________ in the garden one afternoon, a butterfly landed on the page. Several of her friends (5)________ the same series that same week and they talked about it at school. Their teacher reminded them (6)________ at least thirty minutes a day. Nadia sometimes likes to (7)________ her favourite stories when she misses the characters. Right now, Nadia (8)________ her favourite book to her baby sister before bedtime.

D.label: Section D – Vocabulary Cloze
D.passage: Hobbies are a wonderful way to spend free time. Some people enjoy (1)________ activities like painting or sketching, while others prefer (2)________ ones like cycling or swimming. A hobby can also become a (3)________ — something a person is very skilled at after years of practice. Many people find that having a hobby helps reduce (4)________ — the feeling of worry and pressure that builds up during a busy week. The key is to choose something you love and do it with (5)________, not because someone else told you to.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'showed' which is not in the box. EXHIBITED = displayed artworks publicly for others to view.
questions.learning_tip: EXHIBITED = displayed artworks publicly for others to view. Artists EXHIBIT their work in galleries or community centres.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'no two paintings look the same' = originality = creative.
questions.learning_tip: CREATIVE = having the ability to come up with original, imaginative ideas. Making unique paintings = being CREATIVE.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'artwork' which is not in the box. MASTERPIECE = the greatest, most impressive work someone has created.
questions.learning_tip: A MASTERPIECE = the greatest, most impressive work someone has ever created. People call his best painting a MASTERPIECE.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'drew' or 'wrote' which are not in the box. SKETCHED = made a quick rough drawing.
questions.learning_tip: SKETCHED = made a quick, rough drawing. Artists SKETCH ideas in a notebook before starting a full detailed painting.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'reminded him of his happiest memories' = the river gave him the desire to paint = inspired.
questions.learning_tip: INSPIRED = gave someone the desire, enthusiasm or ideas to create something. The river INSPIRED him to paint.

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — here (place) vs hear (to listen)
questions.trap_type: 'here' (place) when 'hear' (ears) is needed.
questions.learning_tip: HEAR = detect sound with ears. HERE = at this place. 'We could HEAR the excitement' → use ears? YES → HEAR. HEAR = ears. HERE = location.

questions.error_type: Spelling — joined (no extra d: join + ed = joined)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'joinded' adding an extra -d. JOIN ends in two consonants (n already) → just add -ed: joined.
questions.learning_tip: JOIN → JOINED (just add -ed). Rule: only double when word ends in ONE vowel + ONE consonant. JOIN ends in -IN (vowel+consonant, but IN has two letters) — actually, N is already there, so just add -ED. JOINED. NEVER 'joinded'.

questions.error_type: Adverb required after action verb (ran)
questions.trap_type: 'quick' (adjective) after action verb 'ran'. A verb needs an adverb.
questions.learning_tip: After an action verb (RAN), use an ADVERB. The children ran QUICKLY = how did they run? QUICKLY (adverb, -ly). 'Quick' describes nouns; 'quickly' describes HOW the action is done.

questions.error_type: Subject-verb agreement — singular subject (one display)
questions.trap_type: 'One display of handmade items' is singular (ONE DISPLAY). Students write 'were' because they see 'items' (plural).
questions.learning_tip: Find the MAIN SUBJECT: 'ONE DISPLAY of handmade items' — the main noun is DISPLAY (singular). ONE DISPLAY WAS knocked over. 'Items' is part of a prepositional phrase, not the main subject. ONE DISPLAY = singular → WAS.

questions.error_type: Possessive apostrophe — plural possessive (students', not students's)
questions.trap_type: Students add 's after apostrophe for plural ending -s.
questions.learning_tip: Plural possessive: add apostrophe AFTER -s! STUDENTS' feedback forms = the forms belonging to all students. NEVER 'students's'. Singular: student's. Plural: students'. Extra -s = WRONG.

E.passage: Last term, our school started a hobby fair where students could share their interests with each other. We could here (1) the buzz of excitement long before we entered the main hall. Mei joinded (2) the photography corner and showed her classmates how to frame a good shot. The children ran quick (3) from one booth to the next, eager to try every activity on offer. One display of handmade items were (4) knocked over during the afternoon session and had to be set up again. At the end of the day, the students's (5) feedback forms were collected and put into a box at the exit.

questions.sentence_a: The photography teacher asked the new members a question.
questions.sentence_b: Do you prefer to photograph people or landscapes?
questions.instruction: Combine into one sentence using reported speech. Begin: 'The photography teacher asked...'
questions.model_answer: The photography teacher asked the new members if they preferred to photograph people or landscapes.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'asked if do they prefer' (wrong order) or keep 'you'.
questions.learning_tip: YES/NO question → reported speech: ASKED + IF + subject + verb (normal order). 'Do YOU prefer?' → asked IF THEY PREFERRED. Pronoun: you → they. Tense: do prefer → preferred. Word order is normal after 'if'.

questions.sentence_a: Kai was building a model ship.
questions.sentence_b: His mother called him for dinner.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'when'.
questions.model_answer: Kai was building a model ship when his mother called him for dinner.
questions.trap_type: Students drop 'was', writing 'Kai building a model ship when his mother called him for dinner'.
questions.learning_tip: Kai WAS BUILDING (ongoing background) when his mother CALLED (sudden event). Keep WAS for the ongoing background action.

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage:
Every Thursday afternoon, the members of Riverside Primary's Photography Club met in Room 12 to review their work and learn new skills. The club had ten members and their teacher-in-charge was Mrs Yeo, a former professional photographer.

One Thursday, Mrs Yeo set them a challenge. 'Next week, I want each of you to bring one photograph that tells a story. No people — only nature.'

Twelve-year-old Ethan spent the whole weekend searching for the perfect shot. On Saturday morning, he noticed dew drops on a spider's web in his garden. He watched patiently as a bee landed in the centre of the web. At exactly the right moment, he pressed the button.

When he developed the photo, Ethan stared at it for a long time. The dew drops sparkled like tiny diamonds. The bee was perfectly in focus. The web stretched across the frame like a delicate net.

The following Thursday, Mrs Yeo looked at all the photos carefully. She held up Ethan's photo for the class to see. 'This one,' she said quietly, 'has a story and a soul.'

Ethan did not fully understand what she meant. But when he looked at the photo again later, he smiled. He did not just take a picture. He captured a moment.

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 1 has the same meaning as 'kept trying without giving up'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: 'Organised' = arranged; 'relaxed' = rested; 'competed' = took part in a contest. PERSISTED = continued trying despite difficulty.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: PERSISTED = kept trying despite difficulty or setbacks. Mei PERSISTED with her photography = she did not give up even when her early photos were not good. PERSIST = keep going; PERSISTED = past tense.

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does 'it' refer to in 'she almost missed it'?

options.2: A brief moment when the old man smiled at a pigeon — the perfect shot Mei captured by waiting patiently
options.4: The school newsletter where the photo would be printed

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking 'it' = the deadline. But 'almost missed IT' = the brief, perfect photographic moment.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: PRONOUN REFERENCE: 'almost missed IT.' IT = the PERFECT MOMENT — the brief instant when the old man smiled at the pigeon. She almost missed IT = the moment was fleeting and she nearly did not capture it. Context: she waited for the right shot.

mcq_questions.stem: What does the teacher mean when she tells Mei 'A great photographer doesn't just take pictures — she sees them first'?

options.1: Great photographers use expensive cameras with special lenses.
options.2: Great photographers plan what to photograph by reading photography books first.
options.3: Great photography begins with the eye and mind — seeing a moment as a picture before the camera clicks.
options.4: Mei should practise drawing before she takes photographs.

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 2 thinking 'sees them first' = reading books. But 'SEES them' = visualising the shot before taking it.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: INFERENCE: 'SEES THEM FIRST' = the photographer VISUALISES the picture in her mind BEFORE pressing the shutter. Great photography = a way of SEEING the world. Option 3 = the teacher is saying photography is as much about PERCEPTION and AWARENESS as it is about the camera.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 1, is it True or False that Mei was immediately good at photography when she joined the club? Give a reason.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: False. The passage says Mei's early photos were blurry and poorly framed — she had to practise for a long time before she improved.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 1: Mei's EARLY PHOTOS WERE BLURRY and POORLY FRAMED. She had to practise and persist before improving. She was NOT immediately good. Answer is FALSE.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Ethan notice in his garden on Saturday morning?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: He noticed dew drops on a spider's web.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'he noticed a bee' — the bee came later. He first noticed the dew drops on the web.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 3: 'he noticed DEW DROPS ON A SPIDER'S WEB.' The bee landing came AFTER he noticed the web.

open_ended_questions.stem: How does the writer describe Ethan's photograph in paragraph 4? Give TWO details.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) The dew drops sparkled like tiny diamonds. (ii) The bee was perfectly in focus. (Accept also: The web stretched across the frame like a delicate net.)
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students describe what Ethan did (stared at it) instead of the visual details of the photograph itself.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 4 gives THREE visual details: dew drops SPARKLED like DIAMONDS, the bee was in FOCUS, the web was like a net. Give any two.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Ethan realise when he looked at his photo again at the end of the passage?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: He realised that he did not just take a picture — he captured a moment.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'he was proud of it' — too general. The passage gives a specific realisation.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Last paragraph: 'He did not just TAKE A PICTURE. He CAPTURED A MOMENT.' This is the specific insight — use those exact words.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on her actions throughout the passage, describe TWO character traits of Mei with evidence.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) PATIENT: Mei waited quietly for the right moment to photograph the old man and the pigeon instead of rushing to press the shutter — showing she understood that the best shot requires waiting. (ii) PERSISTENT: despite her early blurry and poorly framed photos, she kept practising until her work was good enough to win the school competition.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'talented and observant' without precise traits or textual evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: TRAIT INFERENCE: PATIENT = waited for the RIGHT MOMENT, did not rush. PERSISTENT = early photos were BLURRY but she KEPT PRACTISING until she won. Name trait + give evidence from passage = full marks.

questions.stem: The classroom was as ________ as a beehive during group project time — everyone buzzing with ideas.
questions.trap_type: Distractors don't match the comparison. busy = fits the comparison to a beehive.
questions.learning_tip: AS + adj + AS = Simile! Comparing to a beehive. AS + ADJECTIVE + AS is always the correct simile form — never use an adverb.

questions.stem: The students had to ________ information about local animals from books and the internet.
questions.trap_type: 'Invent' means make something up. 'Gather' = collect from different places and bring together.
questions.learning_tip: GATHER = collect from different places and bring together. GATHER information = find and collect facts from books and the internet.

questions.stem: After finishing the experiment, the students had to ________ all the equipment and put it away neatly.
questions.trap_type: Distractors are wrong phrasal verbs. CLEAN UP = tidy or remove dirt and mess.
questions.learning_tip: PHRASAL VERB: CLEAN UP = tidy or remove dirt and mess. These words work together as one meaning — NEVER separate them!

questions.stem: When the team's project won first place, all four members were ________ — they hugged and cheered.
questions.trap_type: Distractors describe different moods. OVER THE MOON = feeling extremely happy and excited.
questions.learning_tip: IDIOM: OVER THE MOON = feeling extremely happy and excited. Idioms cannot be understood word by word — memorise the whole expression!

questions.stem: The class put in a great deal of ________ to complete their model of the solar system before the deadline.
questions.trap_type: 'Rest' is the opposite of working hard. 'Noise' and 'argument' are not positive contributions to a project.
questions.learning_tip: EFFORT = energy and hard work put into doing something. The class put in a lot of EFFORT = worked very hard to finish the model.

questions.stem: Nobody in the class ________ how to solve the science equation without checking the textbook first.
questions.trap_type: NOBODY = singular → verb+S.
questions.learning_tip: NOBODY / EVERYONE / SOMEONE = Singular! Nobody KNOWS = add -S. 'Nobody know' is WRONG. Singular indefinite pronouns always take singular present-tense verbs.

questions.stem: Our class has ________ the most science projects of any class in the school this year.
questions.trap_type: HAS + past participle = present perfect. COMPLETE → COMPLETED (regular).
questions.learning_tip: HAS + past participle = present perfect. Our class HAS COMPLETED the most projects = done so far this year. COMPLETE → COMPLETED (regular verb, add -d).

questions.stem: The students ________ their charts on the board when the principal walked in to observe.
questions.trap_type: 'The principal walked in' = sudden interrupting event. Students were already pasting = past continuous.
questions.learning_tip: The principal WALKED IN = sudden past event. Students were already in the middle of pasting = WERE PASTING (past continuous). Was/were + verb-ing = action in progress when interrupted.

questions.stem: Siva's model was far ________ than anyone else's — it had working lights and moving parts.
questions.trap_type: 'Most impressive' = superlative; 'impressiver' is WRONG. MORE IMPRESSIVE = comparative for long adjectives.
questions.learning_tip: Long adjective (3+ syllables) → MORE + adjective = comparative. MORE IMPRESSIVE THAN = comparing Siva's model to others. 'Impressiver' is ALWAYS WRONG. For long adjectives, use MORE.

questions.stem: Jake missed the science test ________ he was absent from school that day.
questions.trap_type: 'So' reverses the order. 'Because' correctly links the result to its reason.
questions.learning_tip: Missed the test BECAUSE he was absent. BECAUSE = the reason. The reason comes AFTER 'because'.

questions.stem: The science fair was the most exciting event of the school term, ________ it?
questions.trap_type: Positive past 'to be' ('was') → negative question tag. WAS → wasn't it.
questions.learning_tip: Positive past 'to be' → negative tag. The fair WAS exciting, WASN'T it? POSITIVE → NEGATIVE. WAS → WASN'T. Tag questions: match the auxiliary verb of the main clause.

questions.stem: The group finished ________ project two days before the deadline.
questions.trap_type: Before 'project' (a noun), use a possessive adjective. 'They' is a subject pronoun and cannot describe a noun.
questions.learning_tip: Before 'project' (a noun), use a POSSESSIVE ADJECTIVE: THEIR project. 'They project' is wrong.

questions.stem: Although the project was difficult, all the students ________ it on time.
questions.trap_type: The project was completed in the past. 'Submit' is regular: submit → submitted.
questions.learning_tip: Past event. 'Submit' is regular: submit → SUBMITTED. Always check the tense signal.

C.label: Section C – Grammar Cloze (Verb forms of 'write')

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Lina enjoys (1)________ poems in her free time.' Signal: 'enjoys + ___' = gerund (verb-ing). Pattern: enjoy + verb-ing → writing.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'to write' instead of the gerund after 'enjoys'.
questions.learning_tip: ENJOY + verb-ing: enjoys WRITING poems. After 'enjoys', always add -ING.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'She (2)________ in her diary every night before bed.' Signal: 'every night' = regular habit = simple present. Subject 'She' = singular → writes.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'write' (plural form) forgetting that 'She' is a singular subject.
questions.learning_tip: 'Every night' = habit = simple present. She (singular) → WRITES in her diary.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Last week, she (3)________ a poem about the sea for the school competition.' Signal: 'Last week' = past. 'Write' is irregular: write → wrote.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'writed', not knowing 'write' is irregular.
questions.learning_tip: 'Last week' = past. 'Write' is irregular: write → WROTE. Never write 'writed'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'While she (4)________ her final draft, the teacher called her name to present.' Signal: 'While she ___' = ongoing background action in the past. Subject 'she' = singular → was writing. Interrupted by 'the teacher called'.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'wrote' (simple past) missing the ongoing background signal 'while she'.
questions.learning_tip: 'While she ___' = ongoing background past action = past continuous. She WAS WRITING her draft when the teacher called her.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'The other students (5)________ their own drafts at their desks at the same time.' Signal: same past time frame, plural subject 'the other students' + ongoing parallel action → were writing.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'wrote' (simple past) instead of the past continuous for an ongoing parallel action.
questions.learning_tip: The other students = plural. They were doing it at the same moment = WERE WRITING (past continuous).

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Our teacher reminded us (6)________ in full sentences and to check our spelling.' Signal: 'reminded us + ___' = infinitive. Pattern: remind someone + to + base verb → to write.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'writing' instead of the infinitive after 'reminded us'.
questions.learning_tip: 'Reminded us TO + base verb': reminded us TO WRITE in full sentences.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'She always says we should (7)________ from the heart, not just to please others.' Signal: 'should + ___' = modal verb + base form. Never add -s or -ing after a modal.
questions.trap_type: Students add -s or -ing after the modal verb 'should'.
questions.learning_tip: After modal verbs (should, must, can, will), always use the BASE form: should WRITE. Never 'should writes' or 'should writing'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Right now, my friend (8)________ the conclusion of her story for tonight's homework.' Signal: 'Right now' = present continuous. Subject 'my friend' = singular → is writing.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'writes' (simple present habit) missing the 'right now' signal for present continuous.
questions.learning_tip: 'Right now' = present continuous. My friend (singular) → IS WRITING the conclusion right now.

C.passage: Lina enjoys (1)________ poems in her free time. She (2)________ in her diary every night before bed. Last week, she (3)________ a poem about the sea for the school competition. While she (4)________ her final draft, the teacher called her name to present her work to the class. The other students (5)________ their own drafts at their desks at the same time. Our teacher reminded us (6)________ in full sentences and to check our spelling carefully. She always says we should (7)________ from the heart, not just to please others. Right now, my friend (8)________ the conclusion of her story for tonight's homework.

D.label: Section D – Vocabulary Cloze
D.passage: Last term, our class worked on a science project about the water cycle. Each group (1)________ their topic carefully by reading books and watching videos online. Before writing the final report, each group produced a (2)________ first so the teacher could check it. The teacher gave useful (3)________ on each draft, pointing out areas that needed more detail or clearer explanations. The students then made changes to ensure their reports were more (4)________ and complete. On the last day of term, each group (5)________ their findings to the class using posters and a short talk.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'studied' which is not in the box. RESEARCHED = looked into a topic carefully by gathering information.
questions.learning_tip: RESEARCHED = looked into a topic carefully by reading, watching and gathering information from different sources.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'plan' or 'copy' which are not in the box. A DRAFT = a first version of writing that can be improved.
questions.learning_tip: A DRAFT = a first version of writing that can be edited and improved before the final version is submitted.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'advice' which is not in the box. FEEDBACK = comments and suggestions to help someone improve their work.
questions.learning_tip: FEEDBACK = comments and suggestions given to help someone improve their work. The teacher gave FEEDBACK on the drafts.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'detailed' which is not in the box. ACCURATE = correct and free from errors.
questions.learning_tip: ACCURATE = correct and without errors. The teacher's feedback helped make the reports more ACCURATE.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'showed' which is not in the box. PRESENTED = shared work with an audience through speech and visuals.
questions.learning_tip: PRESENTED = shared their work with the class through speech and visual aids. Each group PRESENTED their findings.

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — here (place) vs hear (to listen)
questions.trap_type: 'here' (a place) when the sentence needs 'hear' (ears).
questions.learning_tip: HEAR = detect sound with ears. HERE = at this place. Test: 'We could HEAR the excitement' → can you use your ears? YES → HEAR. HEAR = ears. HERE = location.

questions.error_type: Irregular past — begin → began (not beginned)
questions.trap_type: 'beginned' applies the regular -ed rule. BEGIN is irregular: begin → began.
questions.learning_tip: BEGIN → BEGAN (irregular past). NEVER 'beginned'. Irregular verbs change completely: begin → began, run → ran, sing → sang. Memorise these — they do not follow the -ed rule.

questions.error_type: Irregular invariant verb — cut stays cut in past tense
questions.trap_type: 'cutted' applies regular -ed rule. CUT is invariant: cut → cut.
questions.learning_tip: CUT → CUT (same in past tense). Some verbs do not change at all: cut → cut, put → put, hit → hit, set → set. NEVER 'cutted'. These must be memorised.

questions.error_type: Subject-verb agreement — plural subject (the supplies)
questions.trap_type: 'The supplies' is plural. Students write 'was' (singular).
questions.learning_tip: Plural subject → plural verb! The SUPPLIES WERE = SUPPLIES is plural → WERE. WAS is only for ONE thing. Find the main noun: SUPPLIES = plural → WERE.

questions.error_type: Possessive apostrophe — plural possessive (teachers', not teachers's)
questions.trap_type: Students add 's after apostrophe for a plural noun ending in -s.
questions.learning_tip: Plural possessive: add apostrophe AFTER -s! TEACHERS' comments = the comments from all the teachers. NEVER 'teachers's'. Singular: teacher's. Plural: teachers'. Extra -s after apostrophe = WRONG.

E.passage: Last week, our class worked on a group science project about plants. We could here (1) the excitement in the room as each team started setting up their experiments. One group beginned (2) mixing the soil and seeds too quickly and made a mess. Another team cutted (3) the cardboard pieces into the wrong shapes and had to start again. The supplies was (4) and everyone needed more scissors at the same time. At the end, the teachers's (5) comments were written on a feedback sheet and given to each group.

questions.sentence_a: The teacher asked the class a question.
questions.sentence_b: Have you all finished your part of the project?
questions.instruction: Combine into one sentence using reported speech. Begin: 'The teacher asked...'
questions.model_answer: The teacher asked the class if they had all finished their part of the project.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'asked if have they all finished' (wrong word order) or keep 'you' instead of 'they'.
questions.learning_tip: YES/NO question → reported speech: ASKED + IF + subject + verb (normal order). 'Have YOU all finished?' → asked IF THEY had all finished. Pronoun: you → they. Tense: have → had. Word order is NORMAL after 'if'.

questions.sentence_a: The students were pasting their charts on the board.
questions.sentence_b: The bell rang for recess.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'when'.
questions.model_answer: The students were pasting their charts on the board when the bell rang for recess.
questions.trap_type: Students drop 'were', writing 'The students pasting their charts on the board when the bell rang for recess'.
questions.learning_tip: The students WERE PASTING (ongoing background) when the bell RANG (sudden event). Keep WERE for the ongoing background action.

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage:
It was the last week of term and Class 3C had to complete their science project on insects. Each group had to observe an insect for two weeks, record what they saw and present their findings to the class.

Ten-year-old Maya was in a group with her friends Deen and Siti. Their insect was the ant. Every day after school, the three of them crouched by the ant colony near the school drain and watched carefully.

One afternoon, Siti noticed that the ants were carrying tiny white eggs. 'The queen is moving her eggs to a safer place,' Maya said. She read about this in a library book. Deen quickly took notes while Maya pointed out each ant's role.

On presentation day, their group went last. Maya spoke clearly about the ant colony's structure. Deen explained the roles of the queen, the worker ants and the soldier ants. Siti showed the photographs she took during their observations.

When they finished, Mrs Chen, their science teacher, nodded slowly. 'You three clearly spent a lot of time observing,' she said. 'This is what real science looks like.'

Maya smiled. She started the project thinking insects were boring. She ended it thinking they were one of the most fascinating creatures on Earth.

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 2 has the same meaning as 'carefully watched to check progress'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: 'Ignored' = paid no attention; 'organised' = arranged; 'distributed' = gave out. MONITORED = regularly checked on progress or activity.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: MONITORED = regularly watched or checked to see how something is developing. The teacher MONITORED the groups = she kept an eye on each team's progress throughout the session.

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does 'it' refer to in 'Siva suggested they try it once more'?

options.2: The failed experiment that the group wanted to abandon

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 or 3. 'Try IT once more' = try the experiment again.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: PRONOUN REFERENCE: 'try IT once more.' What had they been doing that failed? The EXPERIMENT. IT = the failed experiment. Siva is encouraging the group not to give up and to attempt the experiment again.

mcq_questions.stem: Why does the writer say Siva 'surprised even himself' when the experiment worked?

options.1: Because Siva usually got everything right without any effort.
options.2: Because Siva had doubted whether he could lead the group to success.
options.3: Because Siva had expected to win first place easily.
options.4: Because no one in the class expected anyone to succeed.

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking he always succeeded. 'Surprised himself' means he doubted his own ability.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: INFERENCE: 'Surprised HIMSELF' = even he did not believe they could succeed. He doubted his own ability. Option 2 = he was uncertain but pushed through. This shows internal doubt overcome by determination.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 1, is it True or False that Siva's group chose their project topic easily? Give a reason.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: False. The passage says the group spent two whole lessons arguing about what to investigate — showing it was not easy at all.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 1: the group SPENT TWO LESSONS ARGUING. ARGUING = disagreeing strongly. This shows it was NOT easy. Answer is FALSE.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did each group member do during the presentation? Name all three roles.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: Maya spoke about the ant colony's structure. Deen explained the roles of the different ants. Siti showed the photographs she took.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students describe only one person's role instead of all three.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 4: MAYA spoke about structure, DEEN explained roles, SITI showed photographs. All three had different roles.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Siti notice one afternoon? What did Maya say about it?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: Siti noticed that the ants were carrying tiny white eggs. Maya said the queen was moving her eggs to a safer place.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students describe only one part — what Siti saw OR what Maya said — instead of both.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 3 has TWO parts: (1) Siti NOTICED the ants carrying EGGS; (2) Maya explained the queen was moving them to a SAFER PLACE. Include both.

open_ended_questions.stem: How did Maya's opinion of insects change from the beginning to the end of the project?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: At the start, Maya thought insects were boring. By the end, she thought they were one of the most fascinating creatures on Earth.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students describe only the end opinion without mentioning how she felt at the start.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Last paragraph: she STARTED thinking insects were BORING and ENDED thinking they were FASCINATING. Always describe both the before and the after.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on his actions throughout the passage, describe TWO character traits of Siva with evidence.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) PERSISTENT: when the experiment failed the first time, Siva suggested they try again rather than giving up — showing he did not quit when faced with difficulty. (ii) ENCOURAGING: he kept the group calm and motivated throughout, praising their efforts even when things went wrong.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'clever and hardworking' without precise traits or evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: TRAIT INFERENCE: PERSISTENT = suggested trying AGAIN after failure. ENCOURAGING = kept group CALM and MOTIVATED. Name trait + give evidence from passage = full marks.

questions.stem: A doctor's work is as ________ as a tightrope walk — one small mistake can have very serious consequences.
questions.trap_type: 'Easy' and 'safe' are opposites. 'Quick' doesn't capture the precision needed. DELICATE = requiring great care and precision.
questions.learning_tip: AS + adj + AS = Simile! A doctor's work is AS DELICATE AS a tightrope walk = comparing the precision required to balancing on a tightrope. DELICATE = requiring extreme care. AS + ADJECTIVE + AS is the correct simile form.

questions.stem: The surgeon had to ________ carefully so that the patient would recover well after the operation.
questions.trap_type: Only 'operate' relates to a surgeon's work. The other words belong to completely different contexts.
questions.learning_tip: To OPERATE = to perform a medical procedure on a patient. A surgeon OPERATES in a hospital theatre.

questions.stem: The plumber decided to ________ the old leaking pipes and replace them with new ones.
questions.trap_type: 'Give in' = surrender; 'run away' = flee; 'put off' = delay. TAKE OUT = remove something from its place.
questions.learning_tip: PHRASAL VERB: TAKE OUT = remove something from where it is fixed or stored. The plumber TOOK OUT the old pipes = he removed them completely. TAKE + OUT work together as one meaning.

questions.stem: When the young chef's dish won first prize at the competition, she was ________ — all her late nights of practice had paid off.
questions.trap_type: 'Under the weather' = ill; 'at a loss' = confused; 'in hot water' = in trouble. ON CLOUD NINE = extremely happy.
questions.learning_tip: IDIOM: ON CLOUD NINE = feeling extremely happy and delighted. She was ON CLOUD NINE = her happiness was at its highest. Idioms cannot be understood word by word!

questions.stem: The lawyer studied all the evidence carefully before ________ her client in court.
questions.trap_type: 'Arresting' is done by police, not lawyers. 'Defending' = arguing in support of someone in a legal case.
questions.learning_tip: DEFENDING = arguing on behalf of someone in a court of law to prove they are not guilty. A defence lawyer DEFENDS her client.

questions.stem: Everyone in the operating theatre ________ completely silent while the surgeon carries out a procedure.
questions.trap_type: EVERYONE = singular → verb+S.
questions.learning_tip: EVERYONE / NOBODY / SOMEONE = Singular! Everyone STAYS = add -S. 'Everyone stay' is WRONG. Singular indefinite pronouns always take singular present-tense verbs.

questions.stem: The head chef has ________ a brand-new menu for the restaurant's grand reopening this month.
questions.trap_type: HAS + past participle = present perfect. CREATE → CREATED (regular).
questions.learning_tip: HAS + past participle = present perfect. The chef HAS CREATED a new menu = done recently and ready now. CREATE → CREATED (regular verb, add -d).

questions.stem: The nurse ________ the patient's temperature when the doctor suddenly called for her assistance.
questions.trap_type: 'The doctor called' = sudden interrupting event. The nurse was already checking = past continuous.
questions.learning_tip: The doctor CALLED = sudden past event. The nurse was already in the middle of checking = WAS CHECKING (past continuous). Was/were + verb-ing = action in progress when interrupted.

questions.stem: The surgeon's hands are far ________ than most people's — years of practice have made them extremely precise.
questions.trap_type: 'Most steady' = superlative; 'more steadier' is WRONG. STEADIER = comparative of 'steady' (short adj ending -y: change y to i, add -er).
questions.learning_tip: Short adjective ending in -Y → change Y to I, add -ER. Steady → STEADIER. 'More steadier' is ALWAYS WRONG. STEADIER THAN = comparing the surgeon's hands to others'.

questions.stem: The pilot landed the plane safely ________ the storm was getting stronger by the minute.
questions.trap_type: 'Because' introduces a reason; 'so' introduces a result. The pilot landing safely despite a storm = a contrast = although.
questions.learning_tip: ALTHOUGH = despite the fact that. The pilot landed safely ALTHOUGH the storm was strong = he succeeded despite the difficulty.

questions.stem: Becoming a doctor takes at least ten years of study and training, ________ it?
questions.trap_type: Positive present simple ('takes') → negative question tag. TAKES → doesn't it.
questions.learning_tip: Positive present simple → negative tag. Becoming a doctor TAKES ten years, DOESN'T it? POSITIVE → NEGATIVE. Present simple → DOES/DOESN'T. 'Doesn't it' (not 'isn't it' — that is for 'to be').

questions.stem: "Please show ________ identification card to the officer at the gate," the guard said.
questions.trap_type: Before a noun ('identification card'), use a possessive adjective. 'You' is a subject pronoun and cannot describe a noun.
questions.learning_tip: Before 'identification card' (a noun), use a POSSESSIVE ADJECTIVE: YOUR identification card. 'You card' is wrong.

questions.stem: The construction workers built the entire bridge ________ without any outside help.
questions.trap_type: 'The construction workers' = they = plural third person → reflexive = themselves. 'Ourselves' = first person plural.
questions.learning_tip: 'The construction workers' = THEY (plural, third person). Reflexive = THEMSELVES. They built it THEMSELVES = without outside help.

C.label: Section C – Grammar Cloze (Verb forms of 'work')

questions.context_check: Passage: 'My father enjoys (1)________ as a paramedic.' Signal: 'enjoys + ___' = gerund (verb-ing). Pattern: enjoy + verb-ing → working.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'to work' instead of the gerund after 'enjoys'.
questions.learning_tip: ENJOY + verb-ing: enjoys WORKING as a paramedic. After 'enjoys', always add -ING.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'He (2)________ at the hospital every day, including weekends.' Signal: 'every day' = regular habit = simple present. Subject 'He' = singular → works.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'work' (plural form) forgetting that 'He' is a singular subject.
questions.learning_tip: 'Every day' = habit = simple present. He (singular) → WORKS at the hospital including weekends.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Last year, he (3)________ a night shift for three months in a row.' Signal: 'Last year' = past. 'Work' is regular: work → worked.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'work' (base form) ignoring the past signal 'Last year'.
questions.learning_tip: 'Last year' = past. 'Work' is regular: work → WORKED.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'While he (4)________ on a difficult case, a second emergency call came in.' Signal: 'While he ___' = ongoing background action in the past. Subject 'he' = singular → was working. Interrupted by 'a second emergency call came in'.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'worked' (simple past) missing the ongoing background signal 'while he'.
questions.learning_tip: 'While he ___' = ongoing background past action = past continuous. He WAS WORKING on a case when the call came in.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Two other paramedics (5)________ alongside him at the same time.' Signal: same past time frame, plural subject 'two other paramedics' + ongoing parallel action → were working.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'worked' (simple past) instead of the past continuous for an ongoing parallel action.
questions.learning_tip: Two other paramedics = plural. They were doing it at the same past moment = WERE WORKING (past continuous).

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Father always wanted (6)________ in a job that helps people.' Signal: 'wanted + ___' = infinitive. Pattern: want + to + base verb → to work.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'working' instead of the infinitive after 'wanted'.
questions.learning_tip: 'Want TO + base verb': wanted TO WORK in a job that helps people. Always use the infinitive after 'wanted'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'He says all paramedics should (7)________ calmly even in the most difficult situations.' Signal: 'should + ___' = modal verb + base form. Never add -s or -ing after a modal.
questions.trap_type: Students add -s or -ing after the modal verb 'should'.
questions.learning_tip: After modal verbs (should, must, can, will), always use the BASE form: should WORK. Never 'should works' or 'should working'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Right now, Father (8)________ the early morning shift at the ambulance station.' Signal: 'Right now' = present continuous. Subject 'Father' = singular → is working.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'works' (simple present habit) missing the 'right now' signal for present continuous.
questions.learning_tip: 'Right now' = present continuous. Father (singular) → IS WORKING the early morning shift right now.

C.passage: My father enjoys (1)________ as a paramedic. He (2)________ at the hospital every day, including weekends. Last year, he (3)________ a night shift for three months in a row. While he (4)________ on a difficult case one evening, a second emergency call came in. Two other paramedics (5)________ alongside him at the same time to manage both situations. Father always wanted (6)________ in a job that helps people in their darkest moments. He says all paramedics should (7)________ calmly even in the most difficult situations. Right now, Father (8)________ the early morning shift at the ambulance station.

D.label: Section D – Vocabulary Cloze
D.passage: My aunt is a nurse at a government hospital. She chose this (1)________ because she wanted to care for sick people and make a difference in their lives. Every day, she puts on her white (2)________ before heading to the ward. She looks after many (3)________ who are recovering from illnesses and operations. The work is demanding and she often comes home (4)________ after a long shift. But she never complains. She is one of the most (5)________ workers I know — she gives her best every single day without fail.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'job' which is not in the box. PROFESSION = a type of work that requires special training or education.
questions.learning_tip: A PROFESSION = a type of work requiring special training. Nursing is a PROFESSION because nurses need years of study and training.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'white... before heading to the ward' = nurses wear a uniform at work.
questions.learning_tip: A UNIFORM = a special set of clothes worn by people in the same job or group. Nurses wear a white UNIFORM.

questions.trap_type: Students may write 'people' which is not in the box. PATIENTS = people receiving medical treatment.
questions.learning_tip: PATIENTS = people who are receiving medical care in a hospital or clinic. A nurse looks after PATIENTS in the ward.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'after a long shift' and 'demanding work' = very tired = exhausted.
questions.learning_tip: EXHAUSTED = extremely tired after a lot of physical or mental effort. Nurses are often EXHAUSTED after a long shift.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'gives her best every single day without fail' = committed and hardworking = dedicated.
questions.learning_tip: DEDICATED = fully committed to a job or cause and working hard for it. A DEDICATED nurse gives her best every single day.

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — here (place) vs hear (to listen)
questions.trap_type: 'here' (place) when the sentence needs 'hear' (ears).
questions.learning_tip: HEAR = detect sound with ears. HERE = at this place. Test: 'We could HEAR the excitement' → use ears? YES → HEAR. HEAR = ears. HERE = location.

questions.error_type: Irregular past — buy → bought (not buyed)
questions.trap_type: 'buyed' applies the regular -ed rule. BUY is irregular: buy → bought.
questions.learning_tip: BUY → BOUGHT (irregular past). NEVER 'buyed'. Irregular verbs change completely: buy → bought, teach → taught, catch → caught. Memorise these — they do not follow the -ed rule.

questions.error_type: Irregular past — take → took (not taked)
questions.trap_type: 'taked' applies the regular -ed rule. TAKE is irregular: take → took.
questions.learning_tip: TAKE → TOOK (irregular past). NEVER 'taked'. Irregular verbs do not follow the -ed rule: take → took, make → made, give → gave. These must be memorised.

questions.error_type: Subject-verb agreement — plural subject (some of the chairs)
questions.trap_type: 'Some of the chairs' is plural. Students write 'was' (singular).
questions.learning_tip: Plural subject → plural verb! SOME OF THE CHAIRS WERE broken = CHAIRS is plural → WERE. Find the main noun: CHAIRS = plural → WERE, not WAS.

questions.error_type: Possessive apostrophe — plural possessive (speakers', not speakers's)
questions.trap_type: Students add 's after apostrophe for plural ending in -s.
questions.learning_tip: Plural possessive: add apostrophe AFTER -s! SPEAKERS' cards = the cards belonging to all the speakers. NEVER 'speakers's'. Singular: speaker's. Plural: speakers'. Extra -s after apostrophe = WRONG.

E.passage: Last Friday, we had a 'Careers Day' at school and many professionals came to speak to us. We could here (1) the excitement in the corridor before the first visitor arrived. A paramedic explained that he buyed (2) his first aid kit while he was still studying. Then a lawyer entered and taked (3) her seat at the front of the hall. Some of the chairs was (4) broken and had to be replaced quickly before the session began. At the end, we signed the speakers's (5) thank-you cards and placed them in individual envelopes.

questions.sentence_a: The interviewer asked the young doctor a question.
questions.sentence_b: Do you enjoy your work at the hospital?
questions.instruction: Combine into one sentence using reported speech. Begin: 'The interviewer asked...'
questions.model_answer: The interviewer asked the young doctor if he enjoyed his work at the hospital.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'asked if does he enjoy' (wrong word order) or keep 'you/your'.
questions.learning_tip: YES/NO question → reported speech: ASKED + IF + subject + verb (normal order). 'Do YOU enjoy YOUR work?' → asked IF HE ENJOYED HIS work. Pronoun: you → he, your → his. Tense: do → did (enjoy). Word order is normal after 'if'.

questions.sentence_a: The road was blocked by an accident.
questions.sentence_b: The ambulance could not reach the hospital on time.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'so'.
questions.model_answer: The road was blocked by an accident, so the ambulance could not reach the hospital on time.
questions.trap_type: Students reverse the clauses, writing 'The ambulance could not reach the hospital on time so the road was blocked by an accident'.
questions.learning_tip: Blocked road = CAUSE. Ambulance could not reach = RESULT. Cause + SO + result. The cause always comes BEFORE 'so'.

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage_title: The Best Job in the World
G.passage:
Nine-year-old Preethi could never make up her mind about what she wanted to be when she grew up. One week she wanted to be a scientist, the next a pilot, and the week after that, a baker.

One afternoon, her school organised a Career Day. Parents came in to talk about their jobs. The first speaker was Mr Hassan, a police officer. He told the students about the importance of keeping the community safe and working as a team.

The second speaker was Dr Lim, a children's doctor. She said the best part of her job was seeing a sick child recover and go home healthy. 'Nothing makes me happier,' she said with a warm smile.

The last speaker was Mrs Gomez, a school librarian. She spoke softly about how books could take a person anywhere in the world. 'Every book I shelve is a door to a new adventure,' she said.

After Career Day, Preethi sat quietly in the garden at home. She thought about all three speakers. Each of them loved what they did. Each of them helped people in a different way.

Preethi picked up the book she was reading and smiled. She still did not know what she wanted to be. But she knew one thing for certain — the best job was the one that made you feel proud every single day.

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 1 has the same meaning as 'moved very quickly because of urgency'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: 'Strolled' = walked slowly; 'waited' = stayed put; 'gathered' = collected. RUSHED = moved very fast because of urgency.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: RUSHED = moved very quickly, driven by urgency or a deadline. The paramedic RUSHED to the scene = she moved fast because every second counted.

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does 'it' refer to in 'she said it was the most rewarding job she had ever done'?

options.2: Being a doctor and caring for patients

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking 'it' = the hospital. But 'it was the most rewarding job' = IT = the work/job itself.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: PRONOUN REFERENCE: 'IT was the most rewarding job.' IT = the JOB of being a doctor. The sentence is about what SHE DOES — her career of caring for patients — not where she works.

mcq_questions.stem: Why does the writer end the passage with the question 'What will you be?'

options.1: Because the writer does not know what job they want.
options.2: To suggest that every reader is capable of becoming whatever they choose to work hard for.
options.3: Because the passage is only about one type of job.
options.4: To prove that being a doctor is the best career.

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 or 4. The question is directed at the reader and opens a possibility.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: INFERENCE: 'What WILL YOU be?' = the question is directed at the READER. It implies that every reader has the potential to choose their own path — the passage is about the value of all occupations. It invites reflection, not prescription.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 1, is it True or False that all the jobs described in the passage are dangerous? Give a reason.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: False. The passage describes many types of jobs — including chefs and teachers — that are not dangerous. Only some, like firefighters and paramedics, involve danger.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 1 lists many jobs: chefs, teachers, firefighters, doctors. Only SOME involve danger. Not ALL are dangerous. Answer is FALSE.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Mrs Gomez say about books?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: She said that every book she shelved was a door to a new adventure.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she liked books' which is too vague. The passage gives a specific quote.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 4: 'Every book I shelve is a DOOR TO A NEW ADVENTURE.' Use the specific words from the passage.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Preethi notice about all three speakers after Career Day? Give TWO things they had in common.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) Each of them loved what they did. (ii) Each of them helped people in a different way.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students describe individual speakers instead of identifying what the three had in common.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 5: (1) 'Each of them LOVED what they did' and (2) 'Each of them HELPED people in a different way.' These are the two things in common.

open_ended_questions.stem: Find a phrase in paragraph 2 that tells us what Mr Hassan said was important about his job.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: 'Keeping the community safe and working as a team.'
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students describe his job title (police officer) instead of quoting the specific phrase about what he valued.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2: Mr Hassan spoke about 'KEEPING THE COMMUNITY SAFE and WORKING AS A TEAM.' Find and quote the specific phrase.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on the passage, describe TWO character traits of the young doctor with evidence.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) DEDICATED: the doctor said she worked night shifts for three years before becoming a fully qualified surgeon — showing she put in sustained effort over a long time. (ii) COMPASSIONATE: she said the most rewarding part of her job was seeing patients recover and return to their families — showing she genuinely cared about others.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'hardworking and kind' without precise traits or evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: TRAIT INFERENCE: DEDICATED = worked night shifts for THREE YEARS. COMPASSIONATE = moved by seeing patients RECOVER and return to families. Name trait + give evidence = full marks.

questions.stem: The lion's roar was as ________ as thunder — every visitor in the zoo stopped what they were doing and turned to look.
questions.trap_type: 'Soft' and 'quiet' are opposites of thunder. 'Distant' = far away. LOUD = producing strong powerful sound.
