As they grow older, grandparents may appear (1)________ in body, moving slowly and tiring easily, but their minds and hearts remain full of experience. The (2)________ they share — lessons about patience, hard work and kindness — is the kind that cannot be learned from a textbook. When grandparents (3)________ about the old days, they are sharing a living piece of family history that would otherwise be lost. These stories form part of a child's cultural (4)________ — a connection to the past that shapes their identity and values. Every family should (5)________ these moments together, for they grow rarer with every passing year.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'moving slowly and tiring easily' = physically weak = frail.
questions.learning_tip: FRAIL = physically weak, especially because of old age. An elderly person may look FRAIL but still be mentally sharp.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'lessons about patience, hard work and kindness that cannot be learned from a textbook' = deep understanding gained through experience = wisdom.
questions.learning_tip: WISDOM = deep understanding and good judgement gained through long experience. Grandparents share WISDOM = valuable life lessons.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'talk about the old days' and 'sharing a living piece of family history' = recall and talk about past memories = reminisce.
questions.learning_tip: REMINISCE = recall and talk about past memories with pleasure and nostalgia. When grandparents REMINISCE, they share stories from their younger days.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'a connection to the past that shapes their identity and values' = cultural background passed down = heritage.
questions.learning_tip: HERITAGE = the cultural background, traditions and values passed down from previous generations. Family stories form part of a child's HERITAGE.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'these moments grow rarer with every passing year' = hold dear and value deeply = cherish.
questions.learning_tip: CHERISH = hold something dear and value it deeply. Every family should CHERISH time with grandparents = treasure these increasingly rare moments.

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — they're (they are) vs their (possessive)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'they're' (they are) when the sentence needs 'their' (belonging to them).
questions.learning_tip: THEIR = belonging to them (possessive adjective before a noun). THEY'RE = they are. 'THEIR stories were amazing' = stories belonging to them. Test: can you replace it with 'they are'? If no, use THEIR.

questions.error_type: Adverb required after action verb (listened)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'patient' (adjective) after the action verb 'listened'. A verb needs an adverb.
questions.learning_tip: After an action verb (listened), use an ADVERB: listened PATIENTLY. 'Patient' is an adjective — it describes nouns, not actions.

questions.error_type: Irregular plural — woman → women
questions.trap_type: Students add -s to 'woman', producing 'womans'. 'Woman' has a completely irregular plural form.
questions.learning_tip: 'Woman' has an irregular plural: woman → WOMEN. Never write 'womans'. Other irregular plurals: man → men, child → children.

questions.error_type: Subject-verb agreement — plural subject (the grandchildren)
questions.trap_type: 'The grandchildren' is plural. Students write 'was' (singular).
questions.learning_tip: 'The grandchildren' = plural → WERE gathered around the table. WAS is only for singular subjects.

questions.error_type: Superlative required when selecting one from a group
questions.trap_type: Students use 'older' (comparative, for two things) when the sentence compares among all the siblings = superlative = oldest.
questions.learning_tip: OLDEST = superlative (comparing among three or more). 'He is the OLDEST of the four brothers' = more than two people being compared → need superlative, not comparative.

E.passage: Last weekend, our whole extended family gathered at Grandma's flat. We listened to they're (1) wonderful stories about life before independence. Grandpa listened patient (2) as each grandchild shared what they were doing in school. He mentioned that in the old days, the womans (3) in his village would wake before sunrise to cook breakfast for the whole family. The grandchildren was (4) gathered around the kitchen table, helping Grandma fold dumplings. Uncle Rajan, who is the older (5) of the four brothers, led everyone in singing a song that Grandma had taught them as children.

questions.sentence_a: My grandfather has been gardening for fifty years.
questions.sentence_b: He knows every plant in the garden by name.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'Since'.
questions.model_answer: Since my grandfather has been gardening for fifty years, he knows every plant in the garden by name.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'My grandfather has been gardening for fifty years since he knows every plant' — reversing the cause and result.
questions.learning_tip: SINCE = because of an ongoing or established fact. SINCE he has been gardening for fifty years, he knows every plant. The reason comes after 'since'.

questions.sentence_a: Grandmother's kueh is the best I have ever tasted.
questions.sentence_b: She has refined her recipe over forty years.
questions.instruction: Combine into one sentence using the relative pronoun 'which'.
questions.model_answer: Grandmother's kueh, which she has refined over forty years, is the best I have ever tasted.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'Grandmother's kueh is the best I have ever tasted which she has refined over forty years' — placing 'which' in the wrong position.
questions.learning_tip: Place 'which' immediately after the noun it refers to. Grandmother's kueh, WHICH she has refined over forty years, is the best I have ever tasted.

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage:
Every Saturday morning, without fail, nine-year-old Nora took the bus to her grandfather's flat in Toa Payoh. It was a fifteen-minute ride she made so many times that she could close her eyes and know exactly when to pull the bell.

Grandpa Lin was always at the door before she knocked. He had a habit of watching for the bus from his kitchen window, and the moment he spotted her yellow school bag through the glass, he would shuffle towards the door.

Their Saturday mornings followed a comfortable routine. Grandpa made kaya toast and soft-boiled eggs while Nora set the table. They ate slowly, and Grandpa told stories — about growing up in a kampung, about his first job at the docks, about the time he cycled from Toa Payoh to Changi just to impress a girl.

'Was that girl Grandma?' Nora always asked.

'Every time,' Grandpa always replied, with a smile that had not changed in forty years.

One Saturday, Nora arrived to find Grandpa asleep in his armchair. She let herself in quietly with the spare key and made the kaya toast herself. When Grandpa woke, he looked at the table and then at her, and something moved across his face that sat between a smile and sadness — something in between.

'You are more like your grandmother every day,' he said.

mcq_questions.stem: How did Grandpa Lin know when Nora was arriving?

options.1: Nora always called him before taking the bus.
options.2: He watched for the bus from his kitchen window.
options.3: He heard her knock on the door.
options.4: Nora's mother sent him a message each time.

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 3 thinking he heard her knock. But the passage says he came to the door BEFORE she knocked — because he watched from the window.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2: 'He had a habit of WATCHING FOR THE BUS FROM HIS KITCHEN WINDOW.' He spotted her BEFORE she knocked — always at the door first.

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 2 has the same meaning as 'walk slowly with short steps'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick 'spotted' (noticed) or 'moment' (a point in time). 'Shuffle' = walk slowly with short, dragging steps.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: SHUFFLE = walk slowly with short, dragging steps, as elderly people often do. Grandpa would SHUFFLE towards the door = walk slowly and carefully.

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 6, what does 'it' refer to in 'it was something in between'?

options.3: Something in between a smile and sadness, like quiet emotion

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking 'it' refers to his eyes. But 'it' refers to the expression on his face — the emotion that was between a smile and sadness.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: In paragraph 6: 'something moved across his face... IT was something in between.' 'It' refers to that expression on his face — neither a smile nor sadness.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 1, is it True or False that Nora had to concentrate on her bus journey to know when to stop? Give a reason from the passage.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: False. The passage says she 'could close her eyes and know exactly when to pull the bell' — she knew the route so well that she did not need to pay attention.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'True, she had to watch the stops carefully.' The passage says the opposite — she knew the route without needing to watch.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 1: she 'could CLOSE HER EYES and know exactly when to pull the bell' = she knew the route by heart and did not need to concentrate. Answer is FALSE.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Nora do when she found Grandpa asleep on the last Saturday described?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: She let herself in quietly with the spare key and made the kaya toast herself.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she woke him up' — she did not. She came in quietly and made breakfast herself.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 6: 'She LET HERSELF IN quietly with the SPARE KEY and made the KAYA TOAST HERSELF.' Two specific actions — she did not wake Grandpa.

open_ended_questions.stem: What TWO specific stories did Grandpa tell during their Saturday mornings? Give examples from paragraph 3.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) He told stories about growing up in a kampung and his first job at the docks. (ii) He told the story about cycling from Toa Payoh to Changi to impress a girl (who turned out to be Grandma).
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students give only one story or say 'he told many stories' without naming specific ones.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 3: (1) growing up in a KAMPUNG / first job at the DOCKS; (2) cycling from Toa Payoh to CHANGI to impress a girl. Give any two specific story topics.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Grandpa mean when he said 'You are more like your grandmother every day'?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: He meant that Nora's actions — letting herself in quietly and preparing breakfast without being asked — reminded him of how his wife used to care for him, showing the same thoughtfulness and love.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she looks like her grandmother' — the passage is about behaviour and character, not physical appearance.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Grandpa saw Nora MAKING BREAKFAST without being asked = caring for him without fuss. This reminded him of GRANDMA's character = quiet, thoughtful love.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on her actions in the passage, describe TWO character traits of Nora with evidence from the passage.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: Nora is a devoted and thoughtful person. Firstly, her devotion is shown by how she visits Grandpa Lin every single Saturday without fail — the passage says she has made the trip so many times that she knows when to pull the bell without looking. Secondly, her thoughtfulness is shown when she finds Grandpa asleep: instead of waking him, she quietly lets herself in and makes the kaya toast herself, showing she puts his comfort first and acts with care rather than convenience.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say she is 'kind and caring' without naming precise character traits or giving specific evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Name precise TRAITS then give EVIDENCE: (1) DEVOTED — visits every Saturday without fail, knows the route by heart; (2) THOUGHTFUL — did not wake Grandpa, QUIETLY made breakfast herself.

questions.stem: The magician ________ a white dove from beneath a silk handkerchief to the audience's delight.
questions.trap_type: 'Destroyed', 'borrowed' and 'swallowed' do not describe producing something in a magic act. 'Produced' = caused something to appear from seemingly nowhere.
questions.learning_tip: PRODUCED = caused to appear or brought out, often in a surprising way. The magician PRODUCED a dove = made it appear from a hidden place.

questions.stem: The magician told the audience he would make the ball ________ and reappear on the other side of the stage.
questions.trap_type: 'Grow' and 'expand' suggest getting bigger; 'bounce' = spring back. Only 'vanish' = disappear suddenly and completely.
questions.learning_tip: VANISH = disappear suddenly and completely. The ball seemed to VANISH from one hand and reappear in another — a classic magic effect.

questions.stem: The audience gasped in ________ as the magician walked through a solid glass panel.
questions.trap_type: 'Boredom', 'sadness' and 'anger' are all inappropriate reactions to a stunning magic trick. 'Disbelief' = shock that something impossible seemed real.
questions.learning_tip: DISBELIEF = the feeling that something cannot be real or true. When the magician walked through glass, the audience gasped in DISBELIEF = they could not believe what they saw.

questions.stem: The magician asked for a ________ from the audience to use in his next trick.
questions.trap_type: 'Stranger', 'enemy' and 'suspect' all have negative connotations. A 'volunteer' = someone who willingly comes forward.
questions.learning_tip: A VOLUNTEER = someone who willingly offers to help or participate. Magicians ask for a VOLUNTEER from the audience to assist with a trick.

questions.stem: A skilled magician ________ the audience's attention with patter and movement so they miss the real trick.
questions.trap_type: 'Removes' and 'rewards' do not describe misdirection. 'Educates' is positive. 'Distracts' = diverts attention away from the real action.
questions.learning_tip: DISTRACTS = draws attention away from something. A magician DISTRACTS the audience = uses talk and movement to make them look the wrong way.

questions.stem: Every year, the school ________ a magic show for students during the end-of-year celebration.
questions.trap_type: 'Every year' = regular habit = simple present. 'The school' is singular → verb needs -s.
questions.learning_tip: 'Every year' = regular habit = simple present. The school (singular) → ORGANISES a magic show each year.

questions.stem: The magician ________ his assistant into a large box and locked it shut with a golden key.
questions.trap_type: Past story. 'Lead' is irregular: lead → led. Students write 'leaded'.
questions.learning_tip: 'Lead' is irregular: lead → LED. The magician LED his assistant into the box = completed past action.

questions.stem: This magic show was ________ than the one we saw at the school carnival last year.
questions.trap_type: Comparing two shows = comparative. 'Exciting' is multi-syllable → use 'more exciting', not 'excitinger'.
questions.learning_tip: COMPARATIVE of multi-syllable adjectives: MORE + adjective. This show was MORE EXCITING than last year's = of the two, this one was better. Never 'excitinger'.

questions.stem: Of all the tricks in the show, the disappearing act was ________ impressive.
questions.trap_type: Superlative needed (comparing among all tricks in the show). 'The most' + adjective = superlative.
questions.learning_tip: SUPERLATIVE: comparing among three or more. Of all the tricks, it was THE MOST IMPRESSIVE = best of all of them. 'The most' + multi-syllable adjective.

questions.stem: There ________ only a little space left at the front of the hall, so some students sat further back.
questions.trap_type: 'A little space' = uncountable singular amount. Past context → was.
questions.learning_tip: 'A little space' = uncountable singular amount. Past event → THERE WAS only a little space left at the front.

questions.stem: The second performance was just ________ spectacular ________ the first one.
questions.trap_type: Equal comparison: 'just as spectacular as' = both performances were equally good.
questions.learning_tip: AS … AS = equal comparison. The second show was just AS SPECTACULAR AS the first = equally impressive.

questions.stem: Three volunteers from the audience ________ to come up to the stage by the magician.
questions.trap_type: The volunteers were the receivers of the action. Past passive = were invited.
questions.learning_tip: The volunteers were the receivers of the action. Past passive = WERE INVITED. Passive = was/were + past participle.

questions.stem: The magician told the audience ________ too loudly so as not to give away the ending of the trick.
questions.trap_type: Negative reported speech: told + object + not to + base verb.
questions.learning_tip: 'Told the audience NOT TO + base verb': told the audience NOT TO REACT too loudly.

C.label: Section C – Grammar Cloze (Verb forms of 'watch')

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Leo loves (1)________ magic shows on video every evening before bed.' Signal: 'loves + ___' = gerund (verb-ing). Pattern: love + verb-ing → watching.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'to watch' instead of the gerund after 'loves'.
questions.learning_tip: LOVE + verb-ing: loves WATCHING magic shows. After 'loves', always add -ING.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'He (2)________ every magician's hand carefully to try to spot the moment the trick happens.' Signal: 'every magician's hand' + habitual action = simple present. Subject 'He' = singular → watches.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'watch' (plural form) forgetting 'He' is singular.
questions.learning_tip: Regular habit = simple present. He (singular) → WATCHES every hand carefully.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Last Friday, Leo (3)________ a live magic show at the community centre for the first time.' Signal: 'Last Friday' = past. 'Watch' is regular: watch → watched.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'watch' (base form) ignoring the past signal 'Last Friday'.
questions.learning_tip: 'Last Friday' = past. 'Watch' is regular: watch → WATCHED.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'While he (4)________ the magician closely, a dove appeared from nowhere and landed on the man's hat.' Signal: 'While he ___' = ongoing background action in the past. Subject 'he' = singular → was watching. Interrupted by 'a dove appeared'.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'watched' (simple past) missing the ongoing signal 'while he'.
questions.learning_tip: 'While he ___' = ongoing background past action = past continuous. He WAS WATCHING closely when the dove appeared.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'His friends (5)________ the same trick from different angles to see if they could spot the secret.' Signal: same past time frame, plural subject 'his friends' + ongoing parallel action → were watching.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'watched' (simple past) instead of past continuous for an ongoing parallel action.
questions.learning_tip: His friends = plural. They were doing it at the same past moment = WERE WATCHING (past continuous).

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Leo wants (6)________ as many different magicians as possible before he turns twelve.' Signal: 'wants + ___' = infinitive. Pattern: want + to + base verb → to watch.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'watching' instead of the infinitive after 'wants'.
questions.learning_tip: 'Want TO + base verb': wants TO WATCH as many magicians as possible. Always use the infinitive after 'wants'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'His teacher says everyone should (7)________ a live magic show at least once in their life.' Signal: 'should + ___' = modal verb + base form. Never add -s or -ing after a modal.
questions.trap_type: Students add -es or -ing after the modal verb 'should'.
questions.learning_tip: After modal verbs (should, must, can, will), always use the BASE form: should WATCH. Never 'should watches' or 'should watching'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Right now, Leo (8)________ a slow-motion recording of the coin trick to see if he can finally figure it out.' Signal: 'Right now' = present continuous. Subject 'Leo' = singular → is watching.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'watches' (simple present habit) missing the 'right now' signal for present continuous.
questions.learning_tip: 'Right now' = present continuous. Leo (singular) → IS WATCHING a slow-motion recording right now.

C.passage: Leo loves (1)________ magic shows on video every evening before bed. He (2)________ every magician's hand carefully to try to spot the moment the trick happens. Last Friday, Leo (3)________ a live magic show at the community centre for the very first time. While he (4)________ the magician closely, a dove appeared from nowhere and landed on the man's hat. His friends (5)________ the same trick from different angles, hoping to catch any movement that would give away the secret. Leo wants (6)________ as many different magicians as possible before he turns twelve. His teacher says everyone should (7)________ a live magic show at least once in their life because no video can capture the feeling of being right there in the room. Right now, Leo (8)________ a slow-motion recording of the coin trick to see if he can finally figure out the secret.

D.label: Section D – Vocabulary Cloze
D.passage: Magic tricks work by fooling the mind rather than actually doing the impossible. The most important tool in a magician's craft is (1)________ of hand — the ability to move objects with the fingers so quickly and smoothly that the eye cannot follow. A magician also uses (2)________ to guide the audience's attention away from what is really happening. For example, a dramatic gesture with one hand draws the eyes while the other hand secretly performs the real action. The result is an (3)________ — a false image that the brain accepts as real because it sees what it expects to see. A skilled magician makes every (4)________ in the audience feel as though the impossible has just happened right in front of them. At the end of some shows, the magician may choose to (5)________ how a trick works, which often surprises audiences — because the method is usually much simpler than they imagined.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'move objects with the fingers so quickly and smoothly that the eye cannot follow' = sleight of hand.
questions.learning_tip: SLEIGHT of hand = the skill of moving your hands and fingers so quickly and cleverly that the eye cannot follow. Magicians practice SLEIGHT of hand for years.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'guide the audience's attention AWAY from what is really happening' = misdirection.
questions.learning_tip: MISDIRECTION = deliberately guiding someone's attention away from what is really happening. Magicians use MISDIRECTION to hide the real secret of the trick.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'a false image that the brain accepts as real' = an illusion.
questions.learning_tip: An ILLUSION = a false image or impression that the mind accepts as real. Magic tricks create ILLUSIONS by exploiting how the brain processes visual information.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'every ___ in the audience feel as though the impossible has just happened' = a person watching = spectator.
questions.learning_tip: A SPECTATOR = a person who watches an event, show or game. Every SPECTATOR in the audience felt the wonder of the trick.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'choose to ___ how a trick works' = to show or disclose the secret = reveal.
questions.learning_tip: REVEAL = to show or disclose something that was previously hidden or secret. Some magicians REVEAL their secrets at the end of a show.

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — to (preposition/infinitive) vs too (also/excessively)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'to' when the meaning is 'excessively' or 'also'. 'Too' = also or excessively.
questions.learning_tip: TOO = also / excessively. 'The trick was TOO fast for us to follow' = excessively fast. TO = towards a destination / infinitive marker. Test: can you replace with 'also' or 'excessively'? If yes, use TOO.

questions.error_type: Adverb required after action verb (watched)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'careful' (adjective) after the action verb 'watched'. A verb needs an adverb.
questions.learning_tip: After an action verb (watched), use an ADVERB: watched CAREFULLY. 'Careful' is an adjective — it describes nouns, not actions.

questions.error_type: Irregular plural — half → halves (f → ves rule)
questions.trap_type: Students add -s to 'half', producing 'halfs'. Words ending in -f often change to -ves in the plural.
questions.learning_tip: 'Half' follows the -f → -ves rule: half → HALVES. Same pattern: leaf → leaves, loaf → loaves, knife → knives.

questions.error_type: Subject-verb agreement — plural subject (the audience members)
questions.trap_type: 'The audience members' is plural. Students write 'was' (singular).
questions.learning_tip: 'The audience members' = plural → WERE stunned. WAS is only for singular subjects.

questions.error_type: Comparative form — 'amazing' already requires 'more', cannot add -er
questions.trap_type: Students add both 'more' AND '-er' to 'amazing', creating 'more amazinger'. Long adjectives use only MORE, not BOTH more + -er.
questions.learning_tip: AMAZING is a multi-syllable adjective: use MORE AMAZING only. Never 'more amazinger' — you cannot use both 'more' AND '-er' on the same adjective.

E.passage: Last Saturday's magic show at the school hall was brilliant. The final trick was to (1) fast for anyone to follow with their eyes. We watched careful (2) as the magician cut the rope into halfs (3) and then magically rejoined it. The audience members was (4) absolutely stunned when the rabbit appeared from the empty hat. Everyone agreed that the second half of the show was more amazinger (5) than the first, and we hoped the school would invite the same magician again next year.

questions.sentence_a: You look closely at the magician's right hand.
questions.sentence_b: You will miss what the left hand is doing.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'As'.
questions.model_answer: As you look closely at the magician's right hand, you will miss what the left hand is doing.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'You look closely as you will miss what the left hand is doing' — reversing the simultaneous/causal relationship.
questions.learning_tip: AS = at the same time that / because. AS you look at the right hand, you WILL MISS the left hand = the two things happen together. 'As' introduces the simultaneous trigger.

questions.sentence_a: You pay attention to the magician's words and movements.
questions.sentence_b: You will be tricked every single time.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'Unless'.
questions.model_answer: Unless you pay attention to the magician's words and movements, you will be tricked every single time.
questions.trap_type: Students add 'will' in the 'unless' clause: 'Unless you will pay attention' — incorrect.
questions.learning_tip: UNLESS + simple present, simple future. UNLESS you PAY attention, you WILL BE tricked. Never 'will' after 'unless'.

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage:
The school hall was full. Three hundred students sat in rows, facing a small stage lit by a single spotlight. On the stage stood a man in a black suit. He introduced himself as Marco.

Marco performed seven tricks that evening. He made a coin pass through a solid table. He caused a handkerchief to change colour three times in a row. He invited a girl named Priya to choose any card from a deck, memorise it and return it to the pack — then he produced it from inside a sealed envelope that sat on a chair since the show began.

But the final trick was the one everyone remembered.

Marco asked the audience to think of any number between one and ten. He did not ask anyone to say it out loud. Then he turned his back to the audience and said, 'The number most of you are thinking of is seven.'

A roar went up from the hall.

Later, a boy named Ethan asked his teacher how the trick worked. 'When people are asked for a number between one and ten,' his teacher said, 'most people choose seven. It's simply how the human brain tends to work.'

Ethan was quiet for a moment. 'So it wasn't really magic at all,' he said.

'Perhaps not,' said the teacher. 'But it felt like it, didn't it?'

mcq_questions.stem: How many tricks did Marco perform in total that evening?
mcq_questions.trap_type: Students may guess a different number. The answer is stated directly in paragraph 2.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2: 'Marco performed SEVEN tricks that evening.' The exact number is clearly stated.

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 2 has the same meaning as 'a set of playing cards'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: Students may pick 'pack' — which is also a correct synonym for a set of cards. However, the question asks for the word IN paragraph 2 that has the same meaning, and 'deck' appears BEFORE 'pack' in the sentence. Both words appear; 'deck' is the first usage.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2: 'choose any card from a DECK' — DECK = a complete set of 52 playing cards. The word 'pack' also appears later in the same sentence and means the same thing.

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 4, what does 'it' refer to in 'He did not ask anyone to say it out loud'?

options.2: The number the audience was thinking of

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 3 thinking 'it' refers to the trick. But the instruction was to 'think of any number' — so 'it' = the number they were thinking of.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 4: Marco asked the audience to 'think of any number between one and ten.' He did not ask them to say IT = THE NUMBER out loud. 'It' = the number they were thinking of.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 2, is it True or False that the sealed envelope was prepared during the show? Give a reason from the passage.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: False. The passage says the envelope 'sat on a chair SINCE THE SHOW BEGAN' — meaning it was placed there before any tricks started, not prepared during the show.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'True, Marco prepared it during the performance.' The envelope was on the chair from the start — before any tricks were performed.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2: the envelope 'had been sitting on a chair SINCE THE SHOW BEGAN.' It was there from the very beginning, not prepared during the act. Answer is FALSE.

open_ended_questions.stem: According to Ethan's teacher, why do most people choose the number seven?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: It is simply how the human brain tends to work — when asked for a number between one and ten, most people naturally think of seven.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'because it is a lucky number' — the passage gives a specific reason about how the BRAIN tends to work.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 6: 'It's simply how the HUMAN BRAIN tends to work.' When asked for a number between one and ten, most brains default to SEVEN.

open_ended_questions.stem: Describe TWO of the tricks Marco performed, using evidence from paragraph 2.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) He made a coin pass through a solid table. (ii) He caused a handkerchief to change colour three times in a row. (Accept also: he produced Priya's chosen card from a sealed envelope.)
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students describe the final trick (the number) which is in paragraph 4, not paragraph 2.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2 gives THREE tricks: (1) coin through a TABLE; (2) handkerchief changing COLOUR; (3) card found in a sealed ENVELOPE. Give any two.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did the teacher mean when she said 'But it felt like it, didn't it?' at the end of the passage?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: She meant that even though the trick was based on psychology rather than real magic, the feeling of wonder and amazement it created was still real and valuable — the experience of magic does not require a supernatural secret.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'the teacher thought it was real magic' — she did not. She meant the FEELING it created was still genuine.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: The teacher means: even if the trick was not 'magic' in the supernatural sense, it still FELT like magic — and that feeling is what matters. The experience of WONDER is real.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on his conversation with his teacher, describe TWO character traits of Ethan with evidence from the passage.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: Ethan is a curious and intellectually honest person. Firstly, his curiosity is shown when he sought out his teacher after the show to ask how the final trick worked — he was not satisfied simply with the experience and wanted to understand the mechanics behind it. Secondly, his intellectual honesty is shown when, upon hearing the explanation, he said plainly 'So it wasn't really magic at all' — he accepted the truth directly rather than choosing to keep believing in something he now knew was not supernatural.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say he is 'smart and questioning' without naming precise character traits or providing specific evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Name precise TRAITS then give EVIDENCE: (1) CURIOUS — ASKED his teacher how the trick worked after the show; (2) INTELLECTUALLY HONEST — accepted the truth plainly ('it wasn't really magic at all').

questions.stem: The students lined up at the starting line, eager to ________ in the relay race.
questions.trap_type: 'Withdraw' means to pull out; 'ignore' and 'cancel' are negative. Only 'participate' = take part actively.
questions.learning_tip: PARTICIPATE = take part actively in an activity. All students were encouraged to PARTICIPATE in Sports Day events.

questions.stem: The coach asked the team to ________ their efforts in the final quarter of the game.
questions.trap_type: 'Reduce' and 'abandon' mean giving up or doing less. 'Double' = increase effort to twice as much when it matters most.
questions.learning_tip: DOUBLE your efforts = increase what you are doing to twice as much. Coaches tell players to DOUBLE their efforts when the game is close.

questions.stem: The runners were ________ at the starting blocks, waiting for the starter's pistol.
questions.trap_type: 'Relaxed' and 'sleeping' suggest they were not ready; 'distracted' means not focused. 'Coiled' = tensed like a spring, ready to burst forward.
questions.learning_tip: COILED = tensed like a spring and ready to release energy. Athletes COIL at the starting blocks = they hold their muscles tight, ready to sprint.

questions.stem: Class 3B showed great ________ by encouraging their teammates even after falling behind.
questions.trap_type: All other options are negative qualities. SPORTSMANSHIP = fair and generous behaviour in sport.
questions.learning_tip: SPORTSMANSHIP = fair, generous and respectful behaviour towards teammates and opponents. Encouraging others even when losing shows great SPORTSMANSHIP.

questions.stem: The anchor runner on the red team ________ the baton and sprinted the final leg to clinch victory.
questions.trap_type: 'Dropped' would lose the race; 'ignored' and 'studied' don't fit the action. SEIZED = grasped quickly and firmly.
questions.learning_tip: SEIZED = grabbed firmly and quickly. The anchor runner SEIZED the baton = took it decisively and ran with it.

questions.stem: Our school has ________ the inter-class relay trophy three years in a row.
questions.trap_type: 'Has won' = present perfect. Students write 'win' or 'wins' ignoring the auxiliary 'has'.
questions.learning_tip: HAS + past participle = present perfect. Our school HAS WON the trophy = it won it at some point and the result stands today.

questions.stem: The students ________ their warm-up exercises when the sky suddenly turned dark.
questions.trap_type: 'The sky turned dark' is the sudden interrupting event. The students were already doing warm-ups = past continuous.
questions.learning_tip: The sky TURNED DARK = sudden past event. Students were already in the middle of warm-ups = WERE DOING (ongoing background).

questions.stem: Running the 4x100m relay is ________ demanding than running a solo 100m sprint.
questions.trap_type: Comparing two events = comparative. 'Demanding' is multi-syllable → MORE, not -er.
questions.learning_tip: COMPARATIVE of multi-syllable adjectives: MORE + adjective. The relay is MORE DEMANDING than the solo sprint = comparing two things.

questions.stem: The PE teacher saw that the students ________ their stretches before any of the events started.
questions.trap_type: The PE teacher SAW = past moment. The students completed stretches before the events = past completed action before another past moment. Simple past is correct here.
questions.learning_tip: The teacher SAW that students COMPLETED their stretches = both actions in the past, simple past for the completed action.

questions.stem: There was ________ energy left in the team after the gruelling morning session.
questions.trap_type: 'Energy' is uncountable → use 'little' or 'much'. 'Few' and 'many' are for countable nouns.
questions.learning_tip: LITTLE = a small amount (uncountable). 'Energy' is uncountable → there was LITTLE energy left. 'Few' is only for countable things you can number.

questions.stem: The winning team has not been announced yet, ________ it?
questions.trap_type: Main clause is NEGATIVE present perfect ('has not been') → POSITIVE question tag. 'Has not' → positive tag = has it.
questions.learning_tip: Negative statement → positive question tag. 'The team HAS NOT been announced, HAS it?' Negative → positive tag.

questions.stem: The gold medal for the long jump event ________ by a student from Class 3C this morning.
questions.trap_type: The medal was the receiver of the action. Past passive = was won.
questions.learning_tip: The gold medal was the receiver of the action. Past passive = WAS WON. Passive = was/were + past participle.

questions.stem: The PE teacher told the students ________ in the sun for too long without drinking water.
questions.trap_type: Negative reported speech: told + object + not to + base verb.
questions.learning_tip: 'Told students NOT TO + base verb': told students NOT TO STAND in the sun without drinking water.

C.label: Section C – Grammar Cloze (Verb forms of 'run')

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Kai loves (1)________ more than any other sport.' Signal: 'loves + ___' = gerund (verb-ing). Pattern: love + verb-ing → running.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'to run' instead of the gerund after 'loves'.
questions.learning_tip: LOVE + verb-ing: loves RUNNING. After 'loves', always add -ING.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'He (2)________ fifty laps every morning before school as part of his training.' Signal: 'every morning' = regular habit = simple present. Subject 'He' = singular → runs.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'run' forgetting 'He' is singular in simple present.
questions.learning_tip: Regular habit = simple present. He (singular) → RUNS fifty laps every morning.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Last Sports Day, Kai (3)________ the anchor leg and helped his team win the relay.' Signal: 'Last Sports Day' = past. 'Run' is irregular: run → ran.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'runned', not knowing 'run' is irregular.
questions.learning_tip: 'Last Sports Day' = past. 'Run' is irregular: run → RAN. Never write 'runned'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'While Kai (4)________ the final stretch, the crowd began to cheer loudly.' Signal: 'while Kai ___' = ongoing background past action. Subject 'Kai' = singular → was running. Interrupted by 'the crowd began to cheer'.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'ran' (simple past) missing the ongoing signal 'while'.
questions.learning_tip: 'While Kai ___' = ongoing background past action = past continuous. Kai WAS RUNNING the final stretch when the crowd cheered.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'His teammates (5)________ alongside him on the track, shouting encouragement.' Signal: same past time frame, plural subject 'his teammates' + ongoing parallel action → were running.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'ran' (simple past) instead of past continuous for an ongoing parallel action.
questions.learning_tip: His teammates = plural. They were doing it at the same past moment = WERE RUNNING (past continuous).

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Kai plans (6)________ in the national school athletics championship next year.' Signal: 'plans + ___' = infinitive. Pattern: plan + to + base verb → to run.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'running' instead of the infinitive after 'plans'.
questions.learning_tip: 'Plan TO + base verb': plans TO RUN in the championship. Always use the infinitive after 'plans'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'His coach says every athlete should (7)________ at least three races before a major competition.' Signal: 'should + ___' = modal verb + base form. Never add -s or -ing after a modal.
questions.trap_type: Students add -s or -ing after the modal verb 'should'.
questions.learning_tip: After modal verbs (should, must, can, will), always use the BASE form: should RUN. Never 'should runs' or 'should running'.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Right now, Kai (8)________ his final practice lap before the championship next week.' Signal: 'Right now' = present continuous. Subject 'Kai' = singular → is running.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'runs' (simple present habit) missing the 'right now' signal for present continuous.
questions.learning_tip: 'Right now' = present continuous. Kai (singular) → IS RUNNING his final practice lap right now.

C.passage: Kai loves (1)________ more than any other sport on the school calendar. He (2)________ fifty laps every morning before school as part of his dedicated training routine. Last Sports Day, Kai (3)________ the anchor leg and helped his team win the relay by a single second. While Kai (4)________ the final stretch, the crowd began to cheer loudly from the sidelines. His teammates (5)________ alongside him on the track, shouting encouragement at every step. Kai already plans (6)________ in the national school athletics championship next year if he qualifies. His coach says every athlete should (7)________ at least three competitive races before a major championship. Right now, Kai (8)________ his final practice lap before the event next week.

D.label: Section D – Vocabulary Cloze
D.passage: Sports Day at Greenfield Primary is one of the most exciting events of the year. Hundreds of (1)________ line the track and field, cheering for their classes and clapping for every athlete who crosses the finish line. In the relay race, each runner must pass a metal (2)________ to the next teammate without dropping it or stepping outside the exchange zone. Athletes who (3)________ in long-distance events need great (4)________ — the ability to keep going when their muscles are tired and their breathing is heavy. Gymnastic events test a different skill: how (5)________ a student can be, moving quickly and gracefully through a series of jumps and rolls.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'line the track and field, cheering for their classes' = people watching = spectators.
questions.learning_tip: SPECTATORS = people who watch an event. Hundreds of SPECTATORS lined the track to cheer for the athletes.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'pass a metal ___ to the next teammate' in a relay race = the object passed between runners = baton.
questions.learning_tip: A BATON = the short stick passed between runners in a relay race. Dropping the BATON in a relay usually means losing the race.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'athletes who ___ in long-distance events' = take part against others = compete.
questions.learning_tip: COMPETE = take part in a contest against others. Athletes COMPETE in long-distance events to test their stamina.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'ability to keep going when muscles are tired and breathing is heavy' = endurance.
questions.learning_tip: ENDURANCE = the ability to keep going for a long time despite fatigue and difficulty. Long-distance runners need great ENDURANCE.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'moving quickly and gracefully through jumps and rolls' = agile.
questions.learning_tip: AGILE = able to move quickly and easily with great coordination. Gymnasts are AGILE — they move their bodies with speed and grace.

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.error_type: Subject-verb agreement — plural subject (the runners)
questions.trap_type: 'The runners' is plural. Students write 'was' (singular).
questions.learning_tip: 'The runners' = plural → WERE all ready at the starting line. WAS is only for singular subjects.

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — their (possessive) vs there (place)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'their' (belonging to them) when the sentence needs 'there' (at that place).
questions.learning_tip: THERE = at that place. The judges stood THERE near the finish line. THEIR = belonging to them. Test: can you replace with 'at that place'? If yes, use THERE.

questions.error_type: Adverb required after action verb (passed)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'quick' (adjective) after the action verb 'passed'. A verb needs an adverb.
questions.learning_tip: After an action verb (passed), use an ADVERB: passed QUICKLY. 'Quick' is an adjective — it describes nouns, not actions.

questions.error_type: Possessive apostrophe — singular possessive (team's, not teams's)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'teams's' adding an extra -s. For a singular noun, add 's: team → team's.
questions.learning_tip: Singular possessive = noun + 's: the TEAM'S captain = the captain of the team. 'Teams's' is wrong — 'teams' is already plural.

questions.error_type: Irregular past tense — run → ran (not runned)
questions.trap_type: Students add -ed to 'run', producing 'runned'. 'Run' is irregular: run → ran.
questions.learning_tip: 'Run' is irregular: run → RAN. Never write 'runned'. Other irregular verbs: swim → swam, sing → sang, throw → threw.

E.passage: On Sports Day, the runners was (1) all lined up at the starting blocks, their hearts pounding with excitement. The judges stood their (2) near the finish line, holding clipboards and stopwatches. During the relay, each runner passed the baton quick (3) to the next teammate without slowing down. After the race, the teams's (4) captain lifted the trophy and thanked everyone for their hard work. Together, they had runned (5) their best race of the year and broken the school record.

questions.sentence_a: You train consistently every week.
questions.sentence_b: You will see a real improvement in your speed.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'As long as'.
questions.model_answer: As long as you train consistently every week, you will see a real improvement in your speed.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'As long as you will train' — adding 'will' after 'as long as', which follows the same rule as 'if'.
questions.learning_tip: AS LONG AS + simple present, simple future. AS LONG AS you TRAIN consistently, you WILL SEE improvement. Never 'will' after 'as long as'.

questions.sentence_a: The relay team trained for six months.
questions.sentence_b: The relay team finally won the district championship.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'After'.
questions.model_answer: After training for six months, the relay team finally won the district championship.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'After the relay team trained for six months, they won' — acceptable, but the model answer shows the more elegant reduction using -ing.
questions.learning_tip: AFTER + verb-ing (same subject): AFTER TRAINING for six months, the team finally WON. When the same subject does both actions, use 'after' + -ing for the first.

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage:
The score between Red House and Blue House was tied at forty-eight points each going into the final event: the 4x100 metre relay. Whoever won this race would win the Sports Day championship.

Red House had the fastest individual sprinter in the school — a girl named Aisha. But the relay is not just about individual speed. The baton must be passed cleanly, and the team must run as one.

Blue House got off to a strong start. Their first two runners built a three-metre lead. By the third leg, the gap had widened to five metres.

Then Aisha stepped onto the track for the final leg. She ran not just with her legs but with everything she had. The crowd went quiet first — then erupted as she closed the gap metre by metre.

With twenty metres to go, she pulled level. With ten, she was ahead.

Red House crossed the finish line first by a fraction of a second.

In the changing room afterwards, Aisha sat quietly. Her teammates expected her to be celebrating. Instead, she said, 'I almost didn't catch up. We need to work on the third handover.'

That is what made her a leader.

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 4 has the same meaning as 'burst out suddenly and loudly'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: 'Quiet' is the opposite; 'closed' means reduced the gap; 'stepped' means moved onto. ERUPTED = burst out suddenly and with great force or noise.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: ERUPTED = burst out suddenly and with great energy or noise. The crowd ERUPTED = broke out in loud cheering all at once.

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does 'it' refer to in 'the gap had widened to five metres'?

options.3: The distance between Blue House and Red House

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking 'it' refers to the race. But 'it' refers to the GAP — the lead Blue House built up.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 3: 'Their first two runners built a three-metre LEAD. By the third leg, IT had widened to five metres.' IT = the gap/lead between the two teams.

mcq_questions.stem: Why did the writer say 'That is what made her a leader' in the last line?

options.1: Because Aisha was the fastest runner in the school.
options.2: Because she had crossed the finish line first.
options.3: Because instead of celebrating, she focused on improving what went wrong.
options.4: Because her teammates listened to everything she said.

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 or 2 thinking being fast or winning makes someone a leader. But the writer points to her THINKING after the victory.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: True leadership is shown in thinking about IMPROVEMENT, not just celebrating victory. Aisha spotted a weakness (the third handover) even after winning — that is what makes a leader.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 6, is it True or False that Red House won the relay by a wide margin? Give a reason from the passage.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: False. The passage says Red House won 'BY A FRACTION OF A SECOND' — a fraction means an extremely small amount of time, not a wide margin.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'True, Red House won clearly.' The passage explicitly says 'by a fraction of a second' = an extremely narrow margin.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 6: 'Red House crossed the line first BY A FRACTION OF A SECOND.' A FRACTION of a second = extremely small. The win was very narrow, not wide. Answer is FALSE.

open_ended_questions.stem: What advantage did Blue House have by the start of the third leg?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: Blue House had a five-metre lead over Red House by the start of the third leg.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'Blue House was winning' without stating the specific gap.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 3: 'by the third leg, the gap had widened to FIVE METRES.' Give the specific measurement from the passage.

open_ended_questions.stem: Paragraph 2 says 'the relay is not just about individual speed.' Explain what this means using TWO ideas from the passage.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) The baton must be passed cleanly between runners — if it is dropped, the team loses. (ii) The team must run as one — everyone's performance matters, not just the fastest runner.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'you need to be fast' — that is exactly what the passage says is NOT the only factor.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2: (1) the BATON must be passed cleanly; (2) the TEAM must run as one. Two specific reasons why relay is about more than individual speed.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Aisha say in the changing room, and how did this surprise her teammates?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: She said 'I almost didn't catch up. We need to work on the third handover.' Her teammates expected her to be celebrating their victory, but instead she focused on a weakness to improve.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she was not happy' — she was not sad either. She was focused on improvement.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 7: teammates expected CELEBRATING, but Aisha talked about the THIRD HANDOVER — a weakness. This surprised them because she focused on improvement, not the win.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on her actions in the passage, describe TWO character traits of Aisha with evidence from the passage.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: Aisha is determined and analytical. (i) DETERMINED: she ran the final leg with a five-metre deficit and closed it to win by a fraction of a second, showing she never gave up. (ii) ANALYTICAL: after the win, she focused on the weak third handover rather than celebrating, showing she always thinks about improvement.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say she is 'fast and kind' without precise traits or evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: DETERMINED — ran with 'everything she had' to close a five-metre gap. ANALYTICAL — spotted the THIRD HANDOVER flaw even after winning.

questions.stem: The removal company arrived early and began to ________ the heavy furniture onto the lorry.
questions.trap_type: 'Paint', 'hide' and 'damage' do not describe moving furniture onto a vehicle. LOAD = place items onto a vehicle for transport.
questions.learning_tip: LOAD = place goods or items onto a vehicle or into a container. The workers LOADED the furniture onto the lorry.

questions.stem: Moving to a new neighbourhood can be ________ at first, but most people settle in within a few weeks.
questions.trap_type: 'Exciting', 'simple' and 'pleasant' are all positive. UNSETTLING = causing feelings of unease or discomfort — the contrast with 'settle in' makes 3 correct.
questions.learning_tip: UNSETTLING = making you feel uneasy or anxious because it disrupts your familiar routine. Moving is often UNSETTLING because everything is unfamiliar.

questions.stem: Mother spent the whole afternoon ________ boxes in the new living room, trying to decide where each item should go.
questions.trap_type: 'Destroying', 'hiding' and 'painting' do not describe organising boxes. STACKING = placing things one on top of another in a neat pile.
questions.learning_tip: STACKING = placing items neatly on top of each other. Mother STACKED the boxes = piled them up in an orderly way.

questions.stem: Father asked the children to ________ the old toys they no longer needed before the move.
questions.trap_type: 'Treasure' = value; 'multiply' = increase; 'break' = damage. SORT OUT = organise and decide what to keep or discard.
questions.learning_tip: SORT OUT = organise things by deciding what to keep, give away or throw away. Before moving, families SORT OUT their belongings.

questions.stem: Despite the chaos of moving, Mother was determined to ________ the new flat before evening so the family could sleep comfortably.
questions.trap_type: 'Abandon' and 'demolish' mean giving up or destroying. 'Renovate' = upgrade. SETTLE IN = make a new place feel comfortable and home-like.
questions.learning_tip: SETTLE IN = make a new place feel like home. Mother wanted to SETTLE IN the new flat = get it organised and comfortable before night.

questions.stem: Our family has ________ to three different flats since I was born.
questions.trap_type: HAS + past participle = present perfect. 'Has moved' = it happened in the past and relates to the present.
questions.learning_tip: HAS + past participle = present perfect. Our family HAS MOVED to three flats = this is the total up to now. 'Move' is regular: move → moved.

questions.stem: The movers ________ the last box when the lift suddenly broke down.
questions.trap_type: 'The lift broke down' = sudden interrupting event. The movers were already carrying = past continuous.
questions.learning_tip: The lift BROKE DOWN = sudden past event. The movers were already in the middle of carrying the box = WERE CARRYING.

questions.stem: Our new flat is ________ than our old one — it has an extra bedroom and a larger kitchen.
questions.trap_type: Comparing two flats = comparative. 'Spacious' is multi-syllable → MORE SPACIOUS. 'Spaciouser' is wrong.
questions.learning_tip: COMPARATIVE of multi-syllable adjectives: MORE + adjective. The new flat is MORE SPACIOUS than the old one. Never 'spaciouser'.

questions.stem: The new neighbourhood doesn't have ________ parks as our old one, but it's closer to the MRT.
questions.trap_type: 'Parks' is countable → use 'as many'. 'Much' is for uncountable. 'AS MANY as' = equal comparison for countable nouns.
questions.learning_tip: AS MANY ... AS = equal comparison for countable plural nouns. The neighbourhood doesn't have AS MANY parks AS the old one. MUCH is for uncountable nouns.

questions.stem: You have been to the new flat before, ________ you?
questions.trap_type: Main clause is positive present perfect ('have been') → negative question tag. 'Have been' → haven't you.
questions.learning_tip: Question tag for positive present perfect: [positive] + HAVEN'T + subject? 'You HAVE been to the flat, HAVEN'T you?' Positive → negative tag.

questions.stem: There ________ much noise from the road, so the family kept the windows closed.
questions.trap_type: 'Much noise' = uncountable singular amount. Past event → was.
questions.learning_tip: 'Much noise' = singular uncountable amount. Past event → THERE WAS much noise from the road.

questions.stem: All the furniture ________ to the new flat within four hours by the removal team.
questions.trap_type: The furniture was the receiver of the action. Past passive = was delivered.
questions.learning_tip: All the furniture was the receiver of the action. Past passive = WAS DELIVERED. Passive = was/were + past participle.

questions.stem: Mother told us ________ in the rooms while the movers were still working.
questions.trap_type: Negative reported speech: told + object + not to + base verb.
questions.learning_tip: 'Told us NOT TO + base verb': told us NOT TO RUN in the rooms while the movers were working.

C.label: Section C – Grammar Cloze (Time prepositions and adverbs)

questions.context_check: Passage: 'We said goodbye to our neighbours (1)________ the removal lorry arrived.' Signal: the goodbye happened earlier than the lorry's arrival = BEFORE. BEFORE = earlier in time than something else.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'after' (later) instead of 'before' (earlier). They said goodbye first, THEN the lorry arrived.
questions.learning_tip: BEFORE = earlier in time than something else. They said goodbye BEFORE the lorry arrived = the goodbye happened first.

questions.context_check: Passage: '(2)________ the last box was loaded, we took one final photo of our old home.' Signal: the photo was taken following the loading = AFTER. AFTER = later in time than something else.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'before' (earlier) instead of 'after' (following). The photo was taken when everything was done.
questions.learning_tip: AFTER = later in time. AFTER the last box was loaded, they took the photo = the photo came after the loading was done.

questions.context_check: Passage: '(3)________ the journey to our new home, I stared out of the window and thought about my old room.' Signal: happening throughout a period/event = DURING. DURING = throughout a particular time or event.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'while' (not in the box) or 'before'. DURING = throughout a defined period or event.
questions.learning_tip: DURING = throughout a particular time or event. DURING the journey = throughout the time of the journey.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'We have lived in the same block (4)________ I was five years old.' Signal: from a past point up to now = SINCE (used with present perfect). SINCE = from a specific point in the past up to now.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'for' (not in the box) or 'during'. SINCE = from a past moment up to now (with present perfect).
questions.learning_tip: SINCE = from a specific past moment up to now. We HAVE lived here SINCE I was five = from that age until now.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'The workers carried boxes (5)________ midnight before they finally finished.' Signal: continuing up to a point in time = UNTIL. UNTIL = up to a point in time.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'before' (already used in blank 1) or 'during'. UNTIL = up to and including that point.
questions.learning_tip: UNTIL = continuing up to a point in time. They worked UNTIL midnight = they kept working all the way up to midnight.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Mother wanted every box unpacked (6)________ the following morning.' Signal: a deadline — completed no later than a specific time = BY. BY = no later than a specific time.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'before' (already used) or 'until'. BY = deadline (finished no later than); UNTIL = duration up to that point.
questions.learning_tip: BY = no later than a specific time (a deadline). Every box unpacked BY morning = done before morning arrives. Different from UNTIL (continuous up to that point).

questions.context_check: Passage: 'By seven in the morning, Mother had (7)________ arranged the kitchen cupboards.' Signal: completed earlier than expected = ALREADY. ALREADY = sooner than expected, used with present or past perfect.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'yet' (expected but not done) instead of 'already' (done sooner than expected). ALREADY = done before a reference point.
questions.learning_tip: ALREADY = done sooner than expected. By seven, Mother had ALREADY arranged the cupboards = she did it earlier than we expected.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Father had not found his reading glasses (8)________ — they were somewhere in the last unpacked box.' Signal: expected but not done up to now = YET. YET = expected to happen but hasn't happened up to now (used in negatives/questions).
questions.trap_type: Students write 'already' (done early) instead of 'yet' (not done, expected). YET = expected but hasn't happened.
questions.learning_tip: YET = expected but not done up to now (used in negatives and questions). Father had NOT found his glasses YET = he expected to find them but hadn't.

C.passage: Moving day was full of surprises. We said goodbye to our neighbours (1)________ the removal lorry arrived. (2)________ the last box was loaded, we took a final photo of our old home. (3)________ the long journey, I stared out of the window. We have lived in the same block (4)________ I was five years old. The workers carried boxes (5)________ midnight to finish the job. Mother wanted every box unpacked (6)________ the next morning. By seven, Mother had (7)________ arranged all the kitchen cupboards. Father had not found his reading glasses (8)________ — they were in the last unpacked box.

D.label: Section D – Vocabulary Cloze
D.passage: Moving house is one of life's most (1)________ tasks — there are so many things to plan, pack and organise that it can feel overwhelming. Families who (2)________ to a different part of Singapore must get used to a new neighbourhood, new transport routes and new neighbours all at once. Before the move, many families choose to have their new flat (3)________, replacing old paint, flooring and fixtures to make the space feel fresh and welcoming. The hardest part for many people is leaving behind places and routines that feel (4)________ — the coffee shop downstairs, the park around the corner, the school nearby. After the move, the new home may feel (5)________ with boxes and furniture in unexpected places, but this usually sorts itself out within a few weeks.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'so many things to plan, pack and organise that it can feel overwhelming' = daunting.
questions.learning_tip: DAUNTING = seeming difficult and discouraging. Moving house is DAUNTING because of the sheer amount of things to do.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'move to a different part of Singapore' = move to a new location = relocate.
questions.learning_tip: RELOCATE = move to a different place, especially a new home or city. Families who RELOCATE must adjust to a new environment.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'replacing old paint, flooring and fixtures to make the space feel fresh' = renovated.
questions.learning_tip: RENOVATED = repaired and improved by replacing old features. A newly RENOVATED flat has fresh paint, new flooring and updated fittings.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'the coffee shop downstairs, the park around the corner' = well known and comfortable = familiar.
questions.learning_tip: FAMILIAR = well known through long experience. We miss places that feel FAMILIAR — places we know well and associate with comfort and routine.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'boxes and furniture in unexpected places' = messy and disorganised = cluttered.
questions.learning_tip: CLUTTERED = filled with too many things in a disorganised way. A home full of unpacked boxes feels CLUTTERED.

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — it's (it is) vs its (possessive)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'it's' (it is) when the sentence needs 'its' (belonging to it). A room and its window = possessive.
questions.learning_tip: ITS = belonging to it (possessive adjective before a noun). 'The room and ITS window' = the window belonging to the room. IT'S = it is. Test: can you replace with 'it is'? If no, use ITS.

questions.error_type: Subject-verb agreement — plural subject (the boxes)
questions.trap_type: 'The boxes' is plural. Students write 'was' (singular).
questions.learning_tip: 'The boxes' = plural → WERE stacked neatly. WAS is only for singular subjects.

questions.error_type: Adverb required after action verb (wrapped)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'careful' (adjective) after the action verb 'wrapped'. A verb needs an adverb.
questions.learning_tip: After an action verb (wrapped), use an ADVERB: wrapped CAREFULLY. 'Careful' is an adjective — it describes nouns, not actions.

questions.error_type: Possessive apostrophe — singular possessive (family's, not familys)
questions.trap_type: Students add -s without an apostrophe for 'family's'. To show possession: family → family's (add 's).
questions.learning_tip: Singular possessive = noun + 's: the FAMILY'S belongings = the belongings belonging to the family. Never write 'familys' (that would be a wrong plural).

questions.error_type: Comparative — consonant+y adjectives: change y→i before -er (tidy → tidier)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'tidyer' without applying the y→i rule. Words ending in consonant+y change y to i before -er.
questions.learning_tip: 'Tidy' ends in consonant + y: change y → i before adding -er. tidy → TIDIER. Same rule: happy → happier, easy → easier, pretty → prettier.

E.passage: On the first morning in our new flat, I woke up and looked at the room and it's (1) bright window facing east. The boxes was (2) stacked along one wall, waiting to be unpacked. Mother wrapped all the fragile items careful (3) in bubble wrap before placing them in the cupboards. Father sorted through the familys (4) old books and magazines, deciding which ones to donate to the community library. By lunchtime, our new home already looked tidyer (5) than it had when we arrived the night before.

questions.sentence_a: You do not visit the new neighbourhood before moving in.
questions.sentence_b: You will feel nervous on the first day.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'Unless'.
questions.model_answer: Unless you visit the new neighbourhood before moving in, you will feel nervous on the first day.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'Unless you will visit' — adding 'will' in the 'unless' clause.
questions.learning_tip: UNLESS + simple present, simple future. UNLESS you VISIT the new neighbourhood before moving in, you WILL FEEL nervous. Never 'will' after 'unless'.

questions.sentence_a: The removal team carried our belongings with great care.
questions.sentence_b: Not a single item was broken.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'Since'.
questions.model_answer: Since the removal team carried our belongings with great care, not a single item was broken.
questions.trap_type: Students reverse the order: 'Not a single item was broken since the removal team carried our belongings' — acceptable but less natural as an emphasis structure.
questions.learning_tip: SINCE = because of a background reason. SINCE the removal team carried everything carefully, not a single item was broken. The cause comes after 'since'.

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage:
The removal lorry pulled away at seven in the evening, leaving the family of four standing in a flat full of boxes. Ten-year-old Zara had not said a word since they arrived.

Her mother noticed. 'It will feel like home soon,' she said.

Zara said nothing. She went to what was now her bedroom and sat on the bare mattress. The walls were white. There were no drawings pinned to them, no shelves of books, no familiar shadows.

Her father appeared in the doorway with a box in his arms. It was labelled 'ZARA — IMPORTANT'. He placed it gently on the floor and left without speaking.

Zara opened it slowly. Inside were her drawing pads, her coloured pencils, her stack of library books and — at the very bottom — a small framed photograph of her and her best friend Chloe, taken at the school garden on the last day of term.

She picked up a pencil and began drawing. First the outline of the window. Then the tree she could see outside. Then, slowly, the room itself.

By nine o'clock, there were three drawings pinned to the white wall.

When her mother came to say goodnight, Zara looked up and said, 'I think I can make this work.'

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 3 has the same meaning as 'well-known and comfortable through long experience'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: 'Bare' = uncovered; 'white' is a colour; 'shadows' = dark shapes. FAMILIAR = known through long experience.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: FAMILIAR = well known and comfortable through long experience. 'No FAMILIAR shadows' = none of the shapes she knew from her old room.

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 4, what does 'It' refer to in 'It was labelled ZARA — IMPORTANT'?

options.3: The box her father was carrying

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking 'It' refers to her father. But her father had 'a box in his arms' — 'It' = the box.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 4: 'Her father appeared with A BOX in his arms. IT was labelled ZARA — IMPORTANT.' IT = the box he was carrying.

mcq_questions.stem: Why did Father leave 'without speaking' after placing the box on the floor?

options.1: He was too tired to talk after the long day of moving.
options.2: He was angry that Zara was not helping to unpack.
options.3: He understood that Zara needed space and that the box would help more than any words could.
options.4: He did not know what was inside the box.

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking he was just tired. But the deliberate, gentle action of leaving the specific 'IMPORTANT' box and then leaving quietly shows emotional intelligence.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Father chose the box labelled 'IMPORTANT' and left GENTLY without speaking — showing he understood Zara needed space, and that her special things would help her more than words.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 2, is it True or False that Zara's mother understood her daughter was upset? Give a reason from the passage.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: True. The passage says 'Her mother NOTICED' — and she spoke to Zara with reassurance, saying 'It will feel like home soon', showing she was aware of Zara's unhappiness.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'False, the mother was too busy unpacking.' The passage explicitly says the mother NOTICED Zara's silence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2: 'Her mother NOTICED.' She said 'It will feel like home soon' — a reassurance. This shows the mother understood and cared. Answer is TRUE.

open_ended_questions.stem: Name THREE items that were inside the box labelled 'ZARA — IMPORTANT'.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: The box contained her drawing pads, her coloured pencils, and her stack of library books. (Accept also: a small framed photograph of her and her friend Chloe.)
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students name only one or two items.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 5: drawing pads, COLOURED PENCILS, LIBRARY BOOKS, and a FRAMED PHOTOGRAPH. Name any three.

open_ended_questions.stem: How did drawing help Zara feel more at home? Give TWO specific details from the passage.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) By nine o'clock, she had three drawings pinned to the white wall — filling the blank space that had reminded her of what was missing. (ii) She drew the view from her new window and the room itself, which shows she began to connect with and accept her new space.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she felt better' without specific details.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 7: THREE DRAWINGS pinned to the WHITE WALL = the blank, unfamiliar room now had something personal in it. Drawing the NEW WINDOW and room = she started to see it as her own.

open_ended_questions.stem: What does Zara's final line — 'I think I can make this work' — tell us about how she is feeling by the end of the passage?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: She is feeling more hopeful and accepting. She no longer feels helpless about the move — she has taken action by drawing and making the space feel her own, and this has given her confidence.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she is happy now' — she is not fully happy yet, but she is hopeful and determined.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: 'I think I CAN MAKE THIS WORK' = she is choosing to adapt rather than give up. This shows she is HOPEFUL and beginning to take ownership of her new home.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on his actions in the passage, describe TWO character traits of Zara's father with evidence.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: Zara's father is perceptive and emotionally intelligent. (i) PERCEPTIVE: he chose the box labelled IMPORTANT — knowing which items would matter most to Zara. (ii) EMOTIONALLY INTELLIGENT: he placed the box gently and left without speaking, giving Zara space to recover in her own way.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'he is kind and caring' without naming precise traits or giving evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: PERCEPTIVE — chose the IMPORTANT box with her valued items. EMOTIONALLY INTELLIGENT — placed it GENTLY, left WITHOUT SPEAKING, giving her space and comfort without pressure.

questions.stem: At first, the skill seemed impossible, but Ben ________ by watching tutorials and practising daily.
questions.trap_type: 'Gave up' is the opposite; 'slept' and 'ignored' are irrelevant. PERSISTED = continued despite difficulty.
questions.learning_tip: PERSISTED = continued trying despite difficulty. Ben PERSISTED = he did not give up, even when progress was slow.

questions.stem: The music teacher ________ the student for holding the violin bow correctly for the first time.
questions.trap_type: 'Scolded' = told off; 'ignored' = paid no attention; 'confused' = made unsure. PRAISED = expressed admiration.
questions.learning_tip: PRAISED = expressed approval and admiration. The teacher PRAISED the student = told her she had done well.

questions.stem: After months of practice, her skills had ________ to a level where she could perform in front of a small audience.
questions.trap_type: 'Faded', 'collapsed' and 'disappeared' all suggest decline. IMPROVED = got better over time.
questions.learning_tip: IMPROVED = got better. After months of practice, her skills IMPROVED = they reached a higher level.

questions.stem: The instructor demonstrated the technique, then asked the students to ________ it step by step.
questions.trap_type: 'Invent' = create something new; 'ignore' and 'destroy' are negative. REPLICATE = reproduce exactly what was demonstrated.
questions.learning_tip: REPLICATE = copy or reproduce something exactly. Students were asked to REPLICATE the instructor's technique = do it the same way she demonstrated.

questions.stem: What sets great learners apart is the ability to learn from failure without becoming ________ by it.
questions.trap_type: 'Motivated', 'inspired' and 'rewarded' are all positive outcomes. DISCOURAGED = made to feel less confident or willing to continue.
questions.learning_tip: DISCOURAGED = made to feel less confident or willing to keep trying. Great learners fail but are not DISCOURAGED — they learn and keep going.

questions.stem: Maya has ________ the piano for three years and can now play a full piece from memory.
questions.trap_type: HAS + past participle = present perfect. Students write 'study' or 'studies' ignoring 'has'.
questions.learning_tip: HAS + past participle = present perfect. Maya HAS STUDIED piano for three years = she started then and continues now.

questions.stem: The students ________ their coding project when the power cut suddenly knocked out all the computers.
questions.trap_type: 'The power cut knocked out the computers' = sudden interrupting event. The students were already finishing = past continuous.
questions.learning_tip: The power cut KNOCKED OUT computers = sudden past event. Students were in the middle of finishing = WERE FINISHING.

questions.stem: Learning to code is far ________ than it looks if you follow a structured programme.
questions.trap_type: Comparative needed. 'Far' intensifies the comparative. 'Easy' → EASIER (one-syllable adjective adds -er).
questions.learning_tip: FAR EASIER THAN = much easier than. 'Easy' is one syllable → EASIER. FAR + comparative = intensified comparison.

questions.stem: There is ________ patience required when learning a new language than when learning a physical skill.
questions.trap_type: 'Patience' is uncountable → use 'more' or 'much'. 'Many', 'a few' and 'several' are for countable nouns.
questions.learning_tip: PATIENCE is uncountable. Comparative quantity for uncountable = MORE. There is MORE patience required = a larger amount is needed.
