open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she was not hungry' — the passage implies she was avoiding people, not that she wasn't hungry.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 3: By lunchtime, TWELVE PEOPLE laughed at the photo. Paragraph 4: 'Nina did not go to the canteen.' She stayed away because she was hurt and likely did not want to face those who laughed.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Mrs Tan do after Nina showed her the screenshot? Give TWO details.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) She took her time looking at the screenshot before responding — showing she took it seriously. (ii) She clearly stated that it was not harmless and that it was not going to continue.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she helped Nina' — too vague. The passage gives specific actions and words.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 8: Mrs Tan TOOK HER TIME looking at the screenshot. Paragraph 9: 'This is NOT A JOKE... NOT HARMLESS... NOT GOING TO CONTINUE.' Two specific responses — careful attention and clear decisive statement.

open_ended_questions.stem: What happened to the post and the fake account by the next morning?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: The post was removed and the fake account was reported.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'the problem was solved' — too vague.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Last paragraph: 'the POST WAS REMOVED and the FAKE ACCOUNT WAS REPORTED.' These are two specific outcomes. Both are needed for a complete answer.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on her words and actions, describe TWO character traits of Mrs Tan with evidence.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) PERCEPTIVE: Mrs Tan noticed Nina was sitting alone and staring at her desk without being told — she spotted that something was wrong just by watching. (ii) DECISIVE: she clearly stated 'it is not going to continue' and by the next morning the post was removed and the account reported — she acted quickly and firmly.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'caring and strict' without precise traits or evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: TRAIT INFERENCE: PERCEPTIVE = NOTICED Nina sitting alone, ASKED HER TO STAY BEHIND. DECISIVE = said 'NOT GOING TO CONTINUE' and by NEXT MORNING post removed + account reported. Name trait → give evidence.

questions.stem: The young athlete's determination was as ________ as steel — nothing could shake her belief in her own dream.
questions.trap_type: 'Weak', 'heavy' and 'cold' do not describe the quality of determination. STRONG = having great power, force or resilience.
questions.learning_tip: AS + adj + AS = Simile! Her determination was AS STRONG AS steel = comparing its unbreakable quality to steel. STRONG = having great power and resilience that cannot be bent or broken.

questions.stem: Great opportunities to follow your dreams come ________, so you must be ready to grab them with both hands when they appear.
questions.trap_type: 'Every day' means frequently; 'out of the blue' = unexpectedly; 'on purpose' = deliberately. ONCE IN A BLUE MOON = very rarely, only once in a long while.
questions.learning_tip: IDIOM: ONCE IN A BLUE MOON = something that happens very rarely, almost never. Opportunities come ONCE IN A BLUE MOON = only very rarely. A 'blue moon' is an extremely rare event — hence the idiom.

questions.stem: At the end of each year, the class would ________ their graduation ceremony with great excitement.
questions.trap_type: 'Forget', 'give up on' and 'run away from' all show negative feelings. LOOK FORWARD TO = feel excited and positive about something coming in the future.
questions.learning_tip: PHRASAL VERB: LOOK FORWARD TO = feel excited and positive about something in the future. They LOOKED FORWARD TO graduation = they were excited and happy anticipating it. LOOK + FORWARD + TO work together.

questions.stem: The young inventor showed great ________ — she turned every failure into a new idea and never stopped trying.
questions.trap_type: 'Silence' = no sound; 'speed' = fast pace; 'caution' = being careful. PERSEVERANCE = continued effort despite difficulty or failure.
questions.learning_tip: PERSEVERANCE = continuing to try despite difficulties or failures. The inventor showed great PERSEVERANCE = she never gave up even when things went wrong. PERSEVERE = keep going; PERSEVERANCE = the quality of doing so.

questions.stem: Her dream was to become a scientist who would ________ life-saving medicines for patients around the world.
questions.trap_type: 'Sell' = exchange for money; 'remove' = take away; 'copy' = imitate. DEVELOP = create or produce something new through research and work.
questions.learning_tip: DEVELOP = create, build or produce something new through effort and research. A scientist DEVELOPS new medicines = she creates them through long study and testing.

questions.stem: No one in the class ________ what they will be doing in twenty years, but everyone has a dream.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'know' thinking 'no one in the class' = many people. NO ONE = singular → verb+S in present tense.
questions.learning_tip: NO ONE / NOBODY / EVERYONE / EACH = Singular! Always use verb+S. No one KNOWS = add -S. 'No one know' is WRONG. Singular indefinite → singular verb in present tense.

questions.stem: Our school has ________ a Young Innovators Award to encourage students who create new ideas.
questions.trap_type: HAS + past participle = present perfect. 'Establish' is regular: establish → established.
questions.learning_tip: HAS + past participle = present perfect. Our school HAS ESTABLISHED an award = it was created at some point and the award exists now. ESTABLISH → ESTABLISHED (regular verb).

questions.stem: Kai's model rocket design is the most ________ project our science teacher has ever seen from a Primary Three student.
questions.trap_type: This is a superlative context ('the most ... ever seen') but the blank comes AFTER 'the most' — so we need the base adjective. THE MOST + base adjective = superlative.
questions.learning_tip: THE MOST + base adjective = superlative. The MOST IMPRESSIVE project = the one that impresses more than all others. NEVER 'more impressive' after 'the most'. 'Impressiver' is always WRONG.

questions.stem: The students ________ their graduation speeches when the principal walked into the hall.
questions.trap_type: 'The principal walked in' = sudden interrupting event. Students were already rehearsing = past continuous.
questions.learning_tip: The principal WALKED IN = sudden past event. Students were already rehearsing = WERE REHEARSING (past continuous). Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing for an action in progress.

questions.stem: There is ________ room for doubt in Priya's mind — she knows exactly what she wants to do with her life.
questions.trap_type: 'Room' (for doubt) is uncountable → use LITTLE. 'Few', 'a few' and 'many' are for countable nouns.
questions.learning_tip: LITTLE + uncountable noun. Room (for doubt) = uncountable → LITTLE room for doubt. 'Few room' is WRONG. LITTLE = not much (for uncountable things).

questions.stem: Chasing your dreams takes courage and hard work, ________ it?
questions.trap_type: Positive present simple ('takes') → negative question tag. 'Takes' (third person singular) → doesn't it.
questions.learning_tip: Positive simple present (third person singular) → negative tag. Chasing dreams TAKES courage, DOESN'T it? DOES → DOESN'T. POSITIVE → NEGATIVE tag.

questions.stem: The award for the most creative project ________ to a student who designed a water purification device last year.
questions.trap_type: The award received the action. Past passive: was/were + past participle.
questions.learning_tip: WAS/WERE + past participle = passive! The award WAS GIVEN = someone gave it; the award received the action. WAS for singular subject.

questions.stem: The careers counsellor asked the students ________ about the subjects that interested them most.
questions.trap_type: Positive reported speech: asked + object + to + base verb.
questions.learning_tip: ASKED someone TO + base verb. The counsellor asked students TO THINK about the subjects they liked. Formula: asked + person + to + verb (base form).

C.label: Section C – Grammar Cloze (Verb 'dream' — 8 forms)

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Every child (1)________ of making a difference in the world one day.' Signal: 'every child' = singular subject, regular habit = simple present. EVERY = singular → dreams.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dream' (base form) instead of 'dreams' (third person singular present). EVERY child = singular → add -S.
questions.learning_tip: Simple present, singular subject (every child) → add -S. Every child DREAMS = regular present, singular. 'Every child dream' is WRONG. EVERY = singular → dreams.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'She spent all of Saturday (2)________ about what it would be like to live on another planet.' Signal: 'spent... (2)___ing' = gerund after SPEND + time. SPEND + time + verb-ing.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'to dream' (infinitive) instead of 'dreaming' (gerund after spend + time).
questions.learning_tip: SPEND + time + verb-ING (gerund). She spent Saturday DREAMING = spent time in the activity of dreaming. 'Spent to dream' is WRONG. SPEND + time + -ING.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Last night, she (3)________ of standing on a stage and accepting a Nobel Prize.' Signal: 'last night' = past tense. DREAM → DREAMED (regular) = simple past.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dreamt' (acceptable irregular past) but 'dreamed' is in the word_box.
questions.learning_tip: DREAM in the past = DREAMED (regular) or dreamt (irregular). Both correct, but DREAMED is in the word_box. 'Last night she DREAMED' = simple past. DREAM → DREAMED.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'While she (4)________ about the future, her teacher noticed she was not paying attention to the lesson.' Signal: WHILE + background ongoing past action = past continuous. Singular subject 'she' → WAS DREAMING.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dreamed' (simple past) instead of 'was dreaming' (past continuous, ongoing background action). 'While' signals the ongoing background.
questions.learning_tip: 'While she ___' = ongoing past background = past continuous. She WAS DREAMING about the future = she was in the middle of daydreaming. The teacher noticed = the interrupting event.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'All the children in the class (5)________ of different futures when the school bell rang to signal the end of the day.' Signal: plural subject 'all the children' + past continuous (while the bell rang) → WERE DREAMING.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'was dreaming' (singular) instead of 'were dreaming' (plural). All the children = plural → WERE.
questions.learning_tip: Plural subject (all the children) + ongoing past = WERE DREAMING. WAS is for singular; WERE for plural. All the children WERE DREAMING = they were all in the middle of daydreaming.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'It is never too early (6)________ big, her teacher always said.' Signal: 'It is ... (6)___' = IT + IS + adjective + TO-INFINITIVE structure. TO + base verb = infinitive.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dreaming' (gerund) instead of 'to dream' (infinitive after 'too early to').
questions.learning_tip: IT IS [adj] + TO + base verb = infinitive structure. It is never too early TO DREAM = infinitive. 'Too early dreaming' is WRONG. TO + base verb = the infinitive form.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Her parents always told her to (7)________ big and never give up on what she wanted.' Signal: TOLD HER TO + base verb = infinitive. Base form follows 'to'.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dreams' (adds -S, but after 'to' only base form is used) instead of 'dream'.
questions.learning_tip: After TOLD HER TO, always use the BASE verb form. Told her TO DREAM = infinitive (to + base). NEVER 'to dreams' or 'to dreaming'. After TO = base form only.

questions.context_check: Passage: 'Many of these children (8)________ of the same future for years to come.' Signal: 'for years to come' = future reference. WILL + base verb = future simple.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'dream' (present) instead of 'will dream' (future). 'For years to come' = future.
questions.learning_tip: 'For years to come' = the future. WILL + base verb = simple future. They WILL DREAM of these futures = they are going to dream of them in the future. WILL DREAM = future simple.

C.passage: Every child (1)________ of making a difference in the world one day. She spent all of Saturday (2)________ about life on another planet. Last night, she (3)________ of standing on a stage and accepting a Nobel Prize. While she (4)________ about the future, her teacher noticed she was not paying attention. All the children (5)________ of different futures when the bell rang to end the day. It is never too early (6)________ big, the teacher always said. Her parents always told her (7)________ big and never give up on her goals. Many of these children (8)________ of the same future for years to come.

D.label: Section D – Vocabulary Cloze
D.passage: Everyone has at least one dream for the future. A strong (1)________ — a deep desire to achieve something great — keeps a person going through hard times. Having a (2)________ — someone you look up to — helps greatly. A good role model can (3)________ you to try harder and reach higher. People who follow their dreams (4)________ to improve themselves every day, setting small goals. Finding your true (5)________ — the activity that excites you most — is the first step toward a future you are proud of.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'a deep desire to achieve something great — keeps a person going through difficult times' = ambition.
questions.learning_tip: AMBITION = a strong desire to achieve something great. AMBITION is what drives you to keep working when things are hard. An AMBITIOUS person has strong AMBITION.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'a person you look up to who shows you what is possible through hard work' = role model.
questions.learning_tip: A ROLE MODEL = a person whose behaviour and values others admire and try to copy. A good ROLE MODEL shows you what is possible and motivates you to do better.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'to try harder and reach higher than you thought possible' = inspire.
questions.learning_tip: INSPIRE = fill someone with the desire and ability to do something great. A role model INSPIRES you = makes you believe you can do more than you imagined.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'to improve themselves every day, setting small goals' = strive (make great efforts).
questions.learning_tip: STRIVE = make great efforts toward a goal. People who follow their dreams STRIVE to improve = they work hard consistently toward something they want.

questions.trap_type: The clue 'the subject or activity that excites you most — first step towards building a future' = passion.
questions.learning_tip: PASSION = a very strong feeling of enthusiasm and love for something. Your true PASSION = the thing that excites you most and makes you feel most alive.

E.label: Section E – Editing

questions.error_type: Subject-verb agreement — plural subject (the students)
questions.trap_type: 'The students' is plural. Students write 'was' (singular).
questions.learning_tip: Plural subject → plural verb! The students WERE inspired by the speaker. WAS is only for ONE (singular). STUDENTS = more than one → WERE.

questions.error_type: Homophone confusion — bare (uncovered/empty) vs bear (to carry/endure)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'bare' (uncovered, empty) when the sentence needs 'bear' (to carry or endure).
questions.learning_tip: BEAR = carry or endure (to bear hardship). BARE = uncovered, empty or plain. 'She could bare the difficulty' → should it be 'endure'? YES → use BEAR. BEAR (endure) ≠ BARE (uncovered).

questions.error_type: Spelling — ie/ei confusion (brief: I before E)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'breif' putting E before I. 'Brief' follows I-before-E: brIEf.
questions.learning_tip: Rule: I before E, except after C! brIEf = I before E ✅. Remember: 'a brIEf PIE break' — brIEf has IE just like PIE. I before E always in this word!

questions.error_type: Adverb required after action verb (spoke)
questions.trap_type: Students write 'confident' (adjective) after the action verb 'spoke'. A verb needs an adverb.
questions.learning_tip: After an action verb (spoke), use an ADVERB: spoke CONFIDENTLY. Rule: verb + adverb (-ly). 'Confident' describes nouns; 'confidently' describes HOW someone speaks.

questions.error_type: Possessive apostrophe — irregular plural possessive ('children' is already plural, so add 's: children's is CORRECT; 'childrens'' is WRONG)
questions.trap_type: This is a REVERSE error check: 'children's' is the CORRECT form. The error in the passage is 'childrens'' which incorrectly treats 'children' as if it were a regular plural.
questions.learning_tip: CHILDREN = irregular plural (no -s). Possessive: CHILDREN'S (add 's). NOT 'childrens'' — 'childrens' is not a word. CHILDREN'S = belonging to children (irregular plural + 's).

E.passage: On the last day of school, a guest speaker came to talk to our class about following your dreams. The students was (1) excited from the moment she walked in — she was a real astronaut who spent six months on the International Space Station. She told us there were moments when she could barely bare (2) the pressure of training, but she kept going because she knew her dream was worth it. She gave a breif (3) overview of life in space before answering questions from the class. When Mei asked her what advice she would give, the astronaut spoke confident (4) and clearly: 'Start with a small goal and build from there.' At the end, we signed the childrens' (5) journal — a book where every student writes down one dream to work toward.

questions.sentence_a: Priya practised her speech every single day.
questions.sentence_b: She became the most confident presenter in the class.
questions.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using 'After'.
questions.model_answer: After practising her speech every single day, Priya became the most confident presenter in the class.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'After Priya practised, she became' — acceptable, but the model uses the more elegant -ing reduction.
questions.learning_tip: AFTER + verb-ing (same subject) = compact and elegant. AFTER PRACTISING her speech every day, Priya BECAME the most confident presenter. Same subject → 'after + -ing' is concise.

questions.sentence_a: The teacher asked Kai a question.
questions.sentence_b: What do you want to be when you grow up?
questions.instruction: Combine into one sentence using reported speech. Begin: 'The teacher asked...'
questions.model_answer: The teacher asked Kai what he wanted to be when he grew up.
questions.trap_type: Students write 'The teacher asked Kai what did he want to be' — keeping question word order. In reported speech, normal word order is used.
questions.learning_tip: WH-question → reported speech: ASKED + WH-word + subject + verb (normal order). 'What DO you WANT to be?' → asked WHAT HE WANTED to be. Word order flips to normal. Do disappears. You → he; grow → grew.

G.label: Section G – Comprehension
G.passage:
On the last afternoon of Primary Three, Mrs Chen did something she never did before.

She handed out a strip of paper to every student and told them to write one sentence: what they wanted to be in twenty years.

The room went quiet. Students bent over their papers. Some wrote quickly, as if they always knew. Others stared at the ceiling, tapping their pencils.

Mrs Chen collected the strips without reading them. She sealed them inside a small envelope and taped it to the back of the classroom door.

'I will give this back to you when you finish Primary Six,' she said. 'By then, some of you will have changed your minds. Some of you will have found something new. And a few of you — maybe one or two — will be doing exactly what you wrote today.'

She smiled. 'But all of you — every single one — will be further along than you are now. That is the only thing I can promise you.'

Ahmed kept looking at the envelope after Mrs Chen turned back to the board. He wrote three words: 'help sick people.' He did not know what that would look like yet. But he meant every word.

mcq_questions.stem: Which word in paragraph 3 has the same meaning as 'written or done quickly without hesitation'?
mcq_questions.trap_type: 'Quietly' = without sound; 'sealed' = closed securely; 'stared' = looked fixedly. QUICKLY = done in a short time, without delay or hesitation.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: QUICKLY = done in a short time, without hesitation. Some students wrote QUICKLY = they knew their answer right away and wrote without pausing. QUICK → QUICKLY (adverb).

mcq_questions.stem: In paragraph 6, what does 'That' refer to in 'That is the only thing I can promise you'?

options.1: That all students will become what they wrote
options.2: That every student will be further along in life than they are now
options.3: That the envelope will be returned in Primary Six
options.4: That one or two students will change their minds

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 3 thinking 'that' = the envelope return. But the promise Mrs Chen makes is about growth — being further along.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 6: 'All of you... will be FURTHER ALONG than you are now. THAT is the only thing I can promise.' THAT = the fact that every student will grow and move forward. Not the envelope — the growth.

mcq_questions.stem: Why did Mrs Chen collect the strips without reading them?

options.1: Because she did not have time to read them that afternoon.
options.2: Because she wanted to preserve each student's private dream without judging it.
options.3: Because the strips were too small to read easily.
options.4: Because she had already read what the students planned to write.

mcq_questions.trap_type: Students pick option 1 thinking it was about time. But the gesture is clearly intentional — she seals them to protect the students' personal dreams.
mcq_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 4: She collected them WITHOUT READING and SEALED them in an envelope. This is intentional — she preserved each dream privately, without judging or commenting. The dream was for the student, not for her.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on paragraph 2, is it True or False that Mrs Chen told the students to write about their favourite subject? Give a reason.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: False. She told them to write 'what they wanted to be in twenty years' — about their future ambitions, not their favourite subject.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'True, she gave them something to write.' She did, but it was about future ambitions, not favourite subjects.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 2: 'what they WANTED TO BE IN TWENTY YEARS.' This is about FUTURE AMBITIONS, not favourite subjects. Answer is FALSE.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Mrs Chen do with the strips of paper after collecting them?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: She sealed them inside a small envelope and taped it to the back of the classroom door, planning to return it to the students in Primary Six.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'she kept them' — too vague. The passage gives two specific details.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 4: She SEALED them inside a small ENVELOPE and TAPED IT TO THE BACK OF THE CLASSROOM DOOR. Both actions are needed for a complete answer.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Mrs Chen promise all the students? Give TWO things she said about what might happen by Primary Six.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) Some students will have changed their minds about what they want to be. (ii) A few students — maybe one or two — will be doing exactly what they wrote that day.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students give only the promise that all will grow — that is the main promise but not the two specific things she mentioned.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Paragraph 5: (1) 'Some of you will have CHANGED YOUR MINDS.' (2) 'A few of you will be doing EXACTLY WHAT YOU WROTE TODAY.' These are two specific predictions she made — use both.

open_ended_questions.stem: What did Ahmed write on his strip of paper, and how did he feel about it?
open_ended_questions.model_answer: Ahmed wrote 'help sick people' — three simple words. He did not know exactly what that would look like yet, but he had meant every word.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'he wanted to be a doctor' — the passage does not say 'doctor'; it says 'help sick people'.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: Last paragraph: Ahmed wrote 'HELP SICK PEOPLE' — exactly three words. He 'DID NOT KNOW WHAT THAT WOULD LOOK LIKE YET' but 'HAD MEANT EVERY WORD.' He was sincere even if unsure of the path.

open_ended_questions.stem: Based on her words and actions, describe TWO character traits of Mrs Chen with evidence.
open_ended_questions.model_answer: (i) THOUGHTFUL: she collected students' strips without reading them and sealed them away — showing she respected each student's private dream. (ii) ENCOURAGING: she promised every single student would be 'further along than you are now' — affirming growth for all, regardless of what they wrote.
open_ended_questions.trap_type: Students say 'kind and caring' without precise traits or evidence.
open_ended_questions.learning_tip: TRAIT INFERENCE: THOUGHTFUL = sealed papers WITHOUT READING = respected their privacy. ENCOURAGING = 'ALL OF YOU will be FURTHER ALONG than you are now' — promised growth for every single student. Name trait → give evidence.
